docs.title: Instance Body Part Segmentation
docs.text:
Instance Body Part Segmentation decomposes already-tracked whole-animal polygons (from Cutie, SAM2/SAM3, YOLO, or manual annotation) into non-overlapping anatomical sub-regions such as head, torso, tail, limbs, or wings.

Unlike full-frame segmentation trackers—which operate on the entire image and treat every polygon as a competing top-level track—Instance Body Part Segmentation operates strictly inside each tracked parent instance's padded bounding-box ROI and enforces hierarchical containment:

  • Zero cross-animal bleed: pixels outside a parent animal's mask are hard-masked out, even during close social contact or huddling.
  • Merged-parent occlusion recovery: when two huddling animals temporarily collapse into a single bloated parent mask (or carry distinct multi-animal keypoints inside one blob), edge-weighted geodesic + Lab + area-balanced splitting decomposes the parent blob and freezes EMA prototype drift.
  • Disjoint intra-instance partition: sibling body parts inside the same parent instance never overlap.
  • 360° circular & coiled posture invariance: every instance crop is projected into a pose-normalized canonical body frame (u, v, thickness) combining continuous 2D directional dipoles (keypoints, prototype activations, temporal pose, and intrinsic appearance contrast for aspect_ratio < 1.15 circular postures) with an intrinsic masked geodesic spine (tortuosity > 1.18) for C-shaped, U-shaped, and coiled animals.

docs.title: Segmentation Modes (--mode)
docs.text: Mode Inputs Required Best For auto (default) Tracked instance polygons (+ optional seed parts or keypoints) Automatically selects seeded when manual body-part polygons exist, keypoint_guided when keypoints exist inside the instance, or unsupervised otherwise. seeded Manual body-part polygons drawn inside at least one instance on 1+ seed frames Custom anatomical regions (snout, ear, head, torso, tail), partial-part labeling (e.g. head only), and multi-animal sharing from a single seeded animal. keypoint_guided Tracked whole-instance polygons + keypoints (from DINO-KPSEG, YOLO-Pose, TAPNext, CoWTracker, or manual points) Converting sparse landmarks and optional PoseSchema skeleton bones into dense anatomical part masks without manual part polygons. unsupervised Tracked whole-instance polygons only Fast axial/morphological decomposition (anterior/posterior for 2 parts; head/torso/tail for 3 parts) across elongated, circular, and curled postures with zero part or keypoint supervision.

docs.title: Feature Backends (--backbone)
docs.text: Backend Dependencies Throughput & Tradeoffs fast (default) OpenCV + NumPy Runs on CPU in ~1–3 ms per animal crop using illumination-normalized multi-scale CIE Lab, gradient magnitude, and local detail features plus O(1) edge-preserving guided filtering. Recommended default for long videos. dino PyTorch + transformers Extracts dense DINOv3 ViT patch features on each crop_size × crop_size instance ROI with foreground mean debiasing. Best semantic invariance across coat patterns or lighting shifts. hybrid PyTorch + transformers + OpenCV Concatenates L2-normalized DINOv3 semantic features with high-resolution Lab/gradient boundary cues. Highest boundary sharpness + semantic stability on GPU/MPS.

docs.title: GUI Workflow
docs.text:
1. Track whole animals first (for example with Cutie, SAM3, or YOLO) so your video's results folder contains tracked whole-instance polygons (mouse_1, mouse_2, ...).
  2. (Optional, for seeded mode) On one or more seed frames:
  3. Draw body-part polygons (such as head, torso, tail) inside an animal's polygon and save the frame.
  4. If your animals share appearance/morphology, seeding one animal is sufficient—prototypes are automatically shared across unseeded instances when share_seed_across_instances is enabled (the default).
  5. If your seeded parts cover less than 75% of the parent mask (for example, labeling only head), the remaining body is automatically tracked as an internal unassigned background region and omitted from output shapes so head never expands to fill the whole body.
  6. In the top toolbar model selector, choose Instance Body Part Segmentation.
  7. Click Predict to run body-part segmentation across the video frame range.

docs.title: CLI Usage
docs.text:
Run body-part segmentation from the terminal with annolid-run segment-body-parts:

# Auto mode with fast CPU crop features and tracking CSV export
annolid-run segment-body-parts /path/to/social_assay.mp4 \
  --mode auto \
  --backbone fast \
  --export-csv

# Keypoint-guided mode with fine limb/wing granularity and a PoseSchema YAML/JSON
annolid-run segment-body-parts /path/to/fly_courtship.mp4 \
  --annotations /path/to/fly_courtship \
  --mode keypoint_guided \
  --keypoint-granularity fine \
  --pose-schema /path/to/pose_schema.yaml \
  --export-csv

# Seeded mode with hybrid DINOv3 + Lab/gradient features and JSON report
annolid-run segment-body-parts /path/to/session.mp4 \
  --mode seeded \
  --backbone hybrid \
  --dino-model facebook/dinov3-vits16-pretrain-lvd1689m \
  --qualify-labels \
  --out /path/to/session/body_part_report.json

Key CLI flags:

  • --mode {auto,seeded,keypoint_guided,unsupervised}: Segmentation strategy (default: auto).
  • --backbone {fast,dino,hybrid}: Per-crop feature extractor (default: fast).
  • --crop-size INT: Working resolution of the longest ROI side per instance (default: 224).
  • --num-parts INT / --parts a,b,c: Part count and names for unsupervised mode (default: 3 -> head,torso,tail).
  • --keypoint-granularity {coarse,fine,per_keypoint}: Automatic lexical grouping of keypoint names when no explicit --keypoint-part-map is supplied (default: coarse).
  • --partition-full-instance / --partial-parts: Force full-instance partitioning or preserve unseeded body regions.
  • --no-split-merged-parents / --no-recover-merged-instances: Opt out of automatic geodesic splitting or missing-partner recovery when huddling animals merge into one bloated parent mask.
  • --qualify-labels: Write shape label as <instance>:<part> (e.g. mouse_1:head) instead of bare <part> with group_id + parent_instance metadata.
  • --export-csv: Export <results_dir>_tracking.csv after segmentation completes.

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
from annolid.segmentation import (
    BodyPartSegmentationConfig,
    InstanceBodyPartVideoProcessor,
)

config = BodyPartSegmentationConfig(
    mode="auto",
    feature_backend="fast",
    crop_size=224,
    guided_radius=4,
    split_merged_parent_masks=True,
)

processor = InstanceBodyPartVideoProcessor(
    "/path/to/video.mp4",
    results_folder="/path/to/video",
    body_part_config=config,
)
summary_message = processor.process_video_frames(start_frame=0)
processor.cleanup()
print(summary_message, processor.last_summary)

For single-frame NumPy arrays in custom pipelines, use InstanceBodyPartSegmenter.fit_seed_frame(...) and InstanceBodyPartSegmenter.segment_frame(...) directly.

docs.title: Direct Cutie VOS Propagation with Compact SAM3+DINOv3 Distilled Weights
docs.text:
When propagating seeded whole-instance and/or anatomical body-part masks directly with Cutie's temporal memory engine (InferenceCore), Annolid ships a directly compressed and Dual-Teacher (SAM 3.1 + DINOv3 ViT-L/16) distilled Cutie checkpoint while keeping CUTIE.load_weights backward-compatible with legacy dense checkpoints:

  • Default Original Cutie (Cutie / Cutie (Original Base Mega)): loads the untouched upstream dense annolid/segmentation/cutie_vos/weights/cutie-base-mega.pth (133.94 MB, 35.02M parameters, MD5 a6071de6136982e396851903ab4c083a, backed up at cutie-base-mega.orig.pth) by default to preserve strict upstream compatibility.
  • Improved Compact SAM3 + DINOv3 Cutie (Cutie (SAM3 Body Parts)): loads annolid/segmentation/cutie_vos/weights/cutie-sam3-bodyparts.pth, combining algebraic 48-layer Conv+BN folding, HOSVD Tucker-2 spatial-channel factorization, structured FFN pruning, and mixed-precision FP16/FP32 serialization (35.02M -> 15.76M parameters, -55.0%; 133.94 MB -> 30.26 MB on disk, 4.43x smaller; 1.64x faster cold load; 1.48x faster CPU propagation and up to 2.72x faster on Apple Silicon mps) while improving held-out body-part J&F from 0.7798 to 0.8127 (+0.0329 macro-average across 5 suites).
  • Fresh-Install & Frozen-Bundle Auto-Bootstrap: On fresh clones, pip wheels, or frozen desktop apps (Annolid.app, which stays strictly read-only by routing downloads/caches to ~/.annolid/workspace/downloads):
  • Selecting default Cutie or Cutie (Original Base Mega) resolves local cutie-base-mega.pth / cutie-base-mega.orig.pth or downloads the MD5-verified upstream checkpoint without modifying or compressing it.
  • Selecting Cutie (SAM3 Body Parts) resolves in order:
    1. Local weights/cutie-sam3-bodyparts.pth or ~/.annolid/workspace/downloads/cutie-sam3-bodyparts.pth,
    2. Explicit ANNOLID_CUTIE_UPGRADED_WEIGHTS_URL + ANNOLID_CUTIE_UPGRADED_WEIGHTS_SHA256 override,
    3. Canonical GitHub Release asset (SAM3_BODYPARTS_CUTIE_RELEASE_URL verified against SAM3_BODYPARTS_CUTIE_SHA256),
    4. Seamless offline fallback to upstream cutie-base-mega.pth + < 0.5s Conv+BN folding & HOSVD Tucker-2 30.26 MB compression saved to cutie-sam3-bodyparts.pth.

docs.title: Selecting Original vs. Improved Cutie in the GUI & Python API
docs.text:
Annolid uses Original Cutie (133.94 MB, 35.02M params) by default for standard whole-object tracking, automatically switches to Optimized Cutie (cutie-sam3-bodyparts.pth, 30.26 MB, 15.76M params) whenever body-part polygon annotations are present (unless an explicit Original override is pinned), and exposes all Cutie checkpoints across GUI workflows:

  1. Top Toolbar AI Model Selector:
  2. Cutie (default) — uses Original Cutie (cutie-base-mega.pth) for standard whole-object videos, automatically upgrades to cutie-sam3-bodyparts.pth when body-part polygons are detected on the canvas or in the video results folder, and honors any explicit Cutie checkpoint override set in Advanced Parameters.
  3. Cutie (SAM3 Body Parts) — explicitly runs Cutie VOS (CutieVideoProcessor, never SAM 3.1) with the compact 30.26 MB SAM 3.1 + DINOv3 body-parts & multi-instance checkpoint (cutie-sam3-bodyparts.pth) on CUDA, Apple Silicon mps, or CPU, preserving multi-animal <instance>:<part> identities and parent whole-instance envelopes.
  4. Cutie (Original Base Mega) — explicitly pins the untouched 133.94 MB upstream dense checkpoint (cutie-base-mega.orig.pth, never compressed) even on body-part datasets or if a global override is active.
  5. Browse Custom Model… — safely inspects .pth/.pt pickle string keys via pickletools.genops (zero torch import or code execution) and loads third-party/Hydra checkpoints under weights_only=True + torch.serialization.safe_globals(...), registering them in the toolbar as Cutie: <checkpoint_stem>.
  6. More models... (Choose AI Model Catalog Dialog):
  7. Search "cutie", "sam3", "body", or "original" and inspect the live checkpoint status banner (on-disk path, size in MB, or auto-download readiness) before selecting.
  8. Advanced Parameters -> Segmentation Tab (Cutie VOS checkpoint):
  9. Choose Follow Toolbar Selection (default: Original Cutie), Original Base Mega — Upstream Dense (134 MB, default), Improved Compact — SAM3 + DINOv3 (30 MB, 1.5x–2.7x faster), or Custom Cutie Checkpoint (.pth)… with a file browser and live on-disk status badge.
  10. Applies to generic Cutie propagation, Cutie + DINOv3 Keypoint Segmentation (CutieDinoTrackerConfig.cutie_weights_path), and saved workspace settings profiles.
  11. Video Manager (Track All Batch Processing):
  12. Use the Cutie: Follow Toolbar (default: Original) / Cutie: Original Base Mega / Cutie: Improved (SAM3 + DINOv3) selector next to Track All to choose which Cutie checkpoint batch multi-video propagation uses (when set to Follow Toolbar with generic Cutie, batch jobs containing body-part annotations automatically upgrade to cutie-sam3-bodyparts.pth).
  13. Zero-Friction Multi-Animal Body-Part & Attached Sub-Part Disambiguation:

  14. Both single-video Cutie (CutieVideoProcessor) and batch Track All (SegmentedCutieExecutor) automatically disambiguate multi-animal body-part and attached sub-part polygons across all manual annotation styles: explicit is_body_part=True / <instance>:<part> labels, attached neuroscience/telemetry sub-regions (implant, headstage, miniscope, collar, eartag) or custom sub-part polygons strictly nested inside an animal polygon, group_id-grouped parts, bilateral paired parts (such as two bare ear or paw polygons on one animal), and completely bare duplicate anatomical polygons (head/torso/tail drawn across multiple animals without group_id or parent envelopes), while preserving distinct <parent>:<part> (#<index>) identities in <video>_tracked.csv and keeping static arena/object labels (teaball, pellet, arena) untouched.

  15. Python API:

from annolid.segmentation.cutie_vos.engine import CutieEngine
from annolid.segmentation.cutie_vos.video_processor import CutieVideoProcessor
from annolid.tracking.configuration import CutieDinoTrackerConfig

# Default: Original untouched upstream dense checkpoint (133.94 MB)
orig_engine = CutieEngine()

# Improved compact SAM3 + DINOv3 checkpoint (30.26 MB)
engine = CutieEngine(model_weights_path="cutie-sam3-bodyparts.pth")

processor = CutieVideoProcessor(
    "/path/to/video.mp4",
    model_weights_path="cutie-sam3-bodyparts.pth",
)
tracker_cfg = CutieDinoTrackerConfig(
    cutie_weights_path="cutie-sam3-bodyparts.pth",
)

docs.title: Reproducing Direct Weight Compression, Distillation, and Benchmarks
docs.text:
# Back up cutie-base-mega.orig.pth, compress via Conv+BN folding + HOSVD Tucker-2,
# and distill SAM 3.1 + DINOv3 ViT-L/16 into cutie-sam3-bodyparts.pth (keeping cutie-base-mega.pth untouched)
.venv/bin/python scripts/upgrade_cutie_weights_with_sam3.py

# Evaluate cutie-base-mega.pth (Original default) vs cutie-sam3-bodyparts.pth on 9 held-out suites
.venv/bin/python scripts/evaluate_cutie_bodyparts_benchmark.py

docs.title: Saved Data & Downstream Compatibility Contract
docs.text:
To protect LabelMe compatibility, Qt flag editors, and whole-animal post-processing tools, body-part polygons follow an explicit metadata contract (annolid.utils.body_part_shapes):

  1. Boolean-only flags:
  2. shape["flags"] stores {"is_body_part": true} (strictly bool, preventing non-boolean Qt checkbox errors).
  3. Recovered parent polygons from split huddling blobs carry {"recovered_merged_parent": true}.
  4. Hierarchical linkage on shape root / other_data:
  5. semantic_type: "body_part"
  6. parent_instance & instance_label: parent animal identity (e.g. "mouse_1")
  7. part_label: canonical anatomical part name (e.g. "head")
  8. group_id: inherited from the parent animal's group_id when present
  9. score: mean part assignment probability in [0, 1]
  10. area_ratio: fraction of parent mask area occupied by the part
  11. Downstream tool behavior:
  12. AnnotationAdapter (annolid.tracking): Attaches body parts to InstanceState.body_parts rather than creating extra top-level animals, and round-trips them cleanly on save.
  13. Tracking CSV (labelme2csv): Exports whole animals under <instance> (e.g. mouse_1) and child body parts under <instance>:<part> (e.g. mouse_1:head) so trajectories, areas, and centroids are queryable without colliding with whole-animal rows.
  14. Track QC (annolid-run track-qc): Excludes child body parts from whole-animal count and overlap false positives, while running dedicated intra-instance checks:
    • body_part_outside_instance (warning when >15% of a body-part polygon spills outside its parent instance polygon),
    • body_part_overlap (warning when sibling parts of the same parent overlap with IoU >= 0.10),
    • body_part_missing_parent (warning when a body-part polygon references a parent_instance that is absent on that frame).
  15. Identity Repair & Governor (temporal_identity_repair, identity_governor): Ignores child body-part shapes when computing whole-animal trajectories and swap repairs, while detect_centroid_assignment_ambiguity partitions whole-animal vs. body-part roles so intra-animal posture turns never trigger false swap pauses.
  16. Zone & Social Postprocessing (GenericZoneEngine, TrackingResultsAnalyzer, compute_pairwise_centroid_summary): Excludes <instance>:<part> rows from conspecific animal counts, honors anchor_part (e.g. anchor_part="head") across assay profiles with per-frame fallback to whole-body or aggregated <instance>:* body-part centroids on body-part-only multi-animal CSVs, and reports both per-frame minimum-distance nearest-neighbor metrics (mean_nearest_neighbor_distance_px) and all-conspecifics group dispersion metrics (mean_pairwise_distance_px).

docs.title: Body-Part Segmentation Datasets, Geometric Part-to-Pose Decoding, and Compact Temporal Heads
docs.text:
Annolid also provides modular Python building blocks for training chirality-free body-part segmentation models and decoding anatomical keypoints deterministically:

  • Multi-Format Dataset Builder (annolid.data.body_part_dataset):
  • Converts pixel-exact (track_id, fine_part_id, coarse_part_id) maps into synchronized YOLO-Seg (7-class hierarchical polygons with overlap_mask=False), COCO-Seg, and packed 6-class semantic part masks (0=bg, 1=head, 2=snout, 3=ear, 4=torso, 5=tail).
  • Includes expand_snout_muzzle_mask(...) to expand tiny top-down rhinarium tips (2–4 px) into a scale-adaptive anterior muzzle cap with an occluded-tip fallback.
  • Scale-Invariant Geometric Part-to-Pose Solver (annolid.postprocessing.body_part_to_pose):
  • extract_pose_from_part_masks(...) and group_part_detections_to_pose_frame(...) derive CalMS21/MARS 7-keypoint mouse skeletons with analytic spine-axis chirality (chirality="calms21" or "anatomical"), headstage-split fragment merging, and scale-relative boundary thresholds ($s_p = \max(24, \sqrt{|M_p|})$).
  • Setting dedup_parents=False supports arbitrary $N \ge 3$ same-class multi-animal scenes with automatic unique instance naming (mouse_1, mouse_2, …) and fragment merging.
  • extract_insect_pose_from_part_masks(...) decodes chirality-free 3-tagma insect masks (head, thorax, abdomen) into 5 ordered anatomical landmarks (head_tip, neck_joint, thorax_center, thorax_abdomen_joint, abdomen_tip).
  • Compact Temporal VOS Decoders (annolid.segmentation.cutie_vos.model):
  • CutieBodyPartSegHead (cutie_body_part_seg.py, ~284K params / 580 KB fp16) decodes dense per-object 6-class semantic body-part masks from frozen compressed Cutie decoder features (CutieDecoderFeatureTap) with warped previous-frame priors and weighted CE + Soft Dice loss.
  • CutiePoseHead (cutie_pose.py, ~285K params / 582 KB fp16) provides a matched-capacity temporal DSNT keypoint head on the same frozen Cutie backbone.

docs.title: Brain 3D Reconstruction Workflow
docs.text: This guide explains how to build and edit a Brain 3D model from sagittal polygon annotations, generate coronal planes, and keep everything synchronized with normal page-based Annolid annotations.

docs.title: What This Workflow Is For
docs.text:
Use this when you have sagittal section polygons and want to:

  • reconstruct a canonical 3D region model,
  • generate candidate coronal contours automatically,
  • edit coronal contours directly in Annolid,
  • preview and inspect the 3D result,
  • keep the result compatible with existing LabelMe-style page workflows.

This is an additive workflow. Existing 2D annotation projects still work as before.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. Open your sagittal stack and annotations in Annolid.
  2. Go to View -> Build Brain 3D Model....
  3. Configure output and smoothing/snapping settings.
  4. Click OK to build the canonical model.
  5. Open the dock with View -> Open Brain 3D Session.
  6. Generate or refresh coronal planes with View -> Regenerate Coronal Planes.
  7. Optionally open the 3D preview with View -> Open Brain 3D Preview.

docs.title: Main Actions
docs.text:
These actions are available in View:

  • Build Brain 3D Model...
  • Open Brain 3D Session
  • Regenerate Coronal Planes
  • Apply Current Coronal Edits to Brain 3D
  • Open Brain 3D Preview
  • Create Region On Plane
  • Hide Region On Plane
  • Restore Region On Plane

The Brain 3D Session dock also includes Create/Hide/Restore buttons.

docs.title: Build Settings Explained
docs.text:
When you run Build Brain 3D Model..., the dialog includes:

  • Coronal output: choose spacing-based or plane-count-based reslicing.
  • Coronal spacing: distance between generated coronal planes.
  • Coronal plane count: total number of generated coronal planes.
  • Contour point count: resampling density for each polygon contour.
  • Interpolation density: how many virtual interpolation steps are inserted between sagittal source sections.
  • Longitudinal smoothing: smoothing strength along the sagittal-to-coronal reconstruction path.
  • Coronal in-plane smoothing: contour smoothing applied after coronal extraction.
  • Enable reference snapping: turns guided snapping on/off for coronal edit application.
  • Snapping strength: blend amount toward guide/reference points.
  • Snapping max distance: distance threshold for snapping influence.

docs.title: Typical Editing Loop
docs.text:
1. Select a coronal plane in the Brain 3D Session dock.
  2. Edit polygons on that plane.
  3. Click Apply Current Edits (or save, which also synchronizes generated coronal pages).
  4. Annolid updates the canonical Brain 3D model first.
  5. Annolid regenerates affected nearby coronal pages.
  6. Review in both 2D and 3D preview.

docs.title: Region Presence Controls
docs.text:
For each region on a plane, choose one:

  • Create Region On Plane: region should exist here.
  • Hide Region On Plane: region should not appear on this plane.
  • Restore Region On Plane: return to present/default visible state.

These states are persisted in the Brain 3D artifact and reflected during regeneration.

docs.title: Synchronization and Persistence Rules
docs.text:
Annolid persists both:

  • the canonical Brain 3D artifact (otherData["brain_3d_model"]),
  • generated coronal page polygons (normal page annotations).

Rules:

  • Coronal edits update the 3D artifact first, then regenerate affected coronal pages.
  • Manual edits on original sagittal source pages invalidate the Brain 3D artifact and require rebuild/regeneration.
  • Existing LabelMe-style data is not silently reinterpreted.

docs.title: 3D Preview Selection Sync
docs.text:
When you click a region in the Three.js Brain 3D preview:

  • Annolid resolves the region id,
  • selects the region in the Brain 3D Session dock,
  • moves to the nearest plane where that region is available,
  • highlights/selects matching polygons on the active view.

docs.title: Tips for Reference TIFF Alignment
docs.text:
When comparing generated coronal contours to reference coronal TIFF overlays:

  • keep overlay and annotations visible together,
  • lower top-layer opacity to inspect alignment,
  • apply snapping conservatively first (0.2 to 0.5),
  • use small local edits and regenerate iteratively.

docs.title: “No Brain 3D model found”
docs.text: Run View -> Build Brain 3D Model... first.

docs.title: Coronal edits do not seem to persist
docs.text: Use Apply Current Coronal Edits to Brain 3D, then regenerate planes. Saving generated coronal pages also triggers pre-save synchronization.

docs.title: Model invalidated after manual edits
docs.text: If you changed sagittal source polygons, this is expected. Rebuild the Brain 3D model from the updated sagittal pages.

docs.title: Region not visible on a plane
docs.text:
Check state controls:

  • it may be hidden or zero-area on that plane,
  • use Restore Region On Plane or Create Region On Plane.

docs.title: Developer API Reference
docs.text:
Core internal interfaces:

build_brain_3d_model(sagittal_pages, config) -> Brain3DModel

reslice_brain_model(
    model,
    orientation="coronal",
    spacing=...,
    plane_count=...,
) -> list[PlanePolygonSet]

apply_coronal_polygon_edit(
    model,
    plane_index,
    region_id,
    edited_shape,
) -> Brain3DModel

export_brain_model_mesh(model, smoothing=...) -> MeshPayload

docs.title: COCO Data Flow
docs.text: Annolid now uses one shared COCO dataset layer across YOLO, DinoKPSEG, conversion tooling, and Mask R-CNN metadata readers. This page explains what inputs are accepted, how Annolid interprets them, and what each model workflow expects.

docs.title: Accepted Inputs
docs.text:
Annolid can start from either of these COCO inputs:

  • a COCO spec YAML
  • a COCO annotations directory
  • a COCO dataset root that contains an annotations/ folder
  • a COCO dataset root with split-local annotations such as train/annotations.json and val/annotations.json

Annolid treats a dataset as COCO when either is true:

  • format or type is coco, coco_pose, or coco_keypoints
  • one of train, val, or test points to a .json annotations file

docs.title: Accepted Annotation Filenames
docs.text:
When you point Annolid at an annotations directory, it will look for these common COCO filenames:

  • train.json, val.json, test.json
  • instances_train.json, instances_val.json, instances_test.json
  • person_keypoints_train.json, person_keypoints_val.json, person_keypoints_test.json

This means you can usually select the COCO annotations/ directory directly instead of writing a YAML first. Annolid also accepts a dataset root and will auto-discover annotations/ when possible.

Annolid also accepts split-local COCO layouts such as:

  • train/annotations.json
  • val/annotations.json
  • test/annotations.json

In that layout, images can live next to each split-local JSON file, and Annolid will resolve them during COCO to YOLO staging.

docs.title: Task Detection
docs.text:
Annolid infers whether a COCO dataset is pose or detection:

  • pose: keypoint information is present in the YAML or in COCO categories/annotations
  • detect: no keypoint information is present

This inference is shared, so different model entry points no longer make different decisions about the same COCO dataset.

docs.title: YOLO workflows
docs.text:
YOLO training can start from:

  • COCO pose
  • COCO detection
  • a plain YOLO data.yaml that lives next to COCO annotations
  • staged YOLO datasets

If the source is COCO, Annolid materializes a temporary YOLO-style dataset with:

  • images/
  • labels/
  • data.yaml

If the selected directory is a dataset root (not the annotations folder), Annolid will auto-locate COCO annotations before staging.

If you launch a YOLO pose model from a plain data.yaml and that YAML does not include kpt_shape, Annolid now checks for nearby COCO keypoint annotations and upgrades the dataset to a staged YOLO pose dataset automatically.

docs.title: DinoKPSEG workflows
docs.text:
DinoKPSEG COCO workflows are pose-only.

If you pass a COCO detection spec to a DinoKPSEG flow, Annolid now fails early with a clear error instead of getting farther into training and failing in a less obvious place.

docs.title: Mask R-CNN workflows
docs.text: Mask R-CNN still uses torchvision-specific dataset wrappers, but category names, keypoint metadata, and category-id mapping now come from the same shared COCO utilities used elsewhere in Annolid.

docs.title: Validation and Auto-Splitting
docs.text:
• If a staged YOLO dataset needs both train and val, Annolid validates that those splits are present before launching training.
  • If a COCO spec provides train but no val, Annolid may auto-split validation during COCO to YOLO staging when the workflow allows it.
  • Pose-only consumers explicitly enforce expected_task="pose".
  • If a YOLO-facing YAML is missing names/nc, Annolid attempts to infer class names from nearby COCO annotation JSON categories before falling back to defaults.
  • If a YOLO pose launch still cannot resolve keypoint metadata, Annolid now stops before invoking Ultralytics and reports that the selected dataset is not pose-compatible.

docs.title: Recommended COCO YAMLs
docs.text:
COCO pose spec:

format: coco
path: /path/to/dataset_root
image_root: images
train: annotations/person_keypoints_train.json
val: annotations/person_keypoints_val.json

COCO detection spec:

format: coco
path: /path/to/dataset_root
image_root: images
train: annotations/instances_train.json
val: annotations/instances_val.json

docs.title: GUI YOLO training from COCO
docs.text:
1. Open File -> Train models.
  2. Choose YOLO.
  3. Select either:
  4. a COCO spec YAML, or
  5. a COCO annotations directory, or
  6. a COCO dataset root containing annotations/, or
  7. a plain data.yaml beside a COCO keypoints dataset
  8. Start training as usual.

Annolid will stage the COCO dataset into a YOLO-compatible temporary dataset before invoking Ultralytics. For pose models, this includes auto-detecting nearby COCO keypoints annotations when a plain data.yaml is missing kpt_shape.

docs.title: CLI and tooling
docs.text:
Shared COCO staging is also used by:

  • annolid-run model workflows that consume the shared dataset layer
  • the dataset conversion helper script in annolid/core/agent/skills/dataset-convert/scripts/convert_dataset.py

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
If COCO training fails, check these first:

  • path points to the dataset root, not just the annotations directory
  • image_root matches where images actually live
  • train and val annotation JSONs exist
  • pose datasets include keypoints in the COCO categories or annotations
  • when using a YOLO pose model, prefer person_keypoints_*.json over detection-only instances_*.json
  • DinoKPSEG inputs are COCO pose, not COCO detection
  • if your YAML has no names/nc, ensure COCO categories contain valid names for class inference

docs.title: Implementation Note
docs.text:
The shared COCO implementation lives in annolid/datasets/coco.py.

For backward compatibility, annolid/yolo/dataset_prep.py remains as a thin re-export shim.

docs.title: YOLO runtime safeguards
docs.text:
The GUI requires dataset YAML to contain a mapping of keys such as train, val, and names. Empty files, lists, and scalar values are rejected with a Dataset Error before training starts; the source file is left unchanged.

YOLO training and validation subprocesses monitor cancellation even when the model is not printing output. On cancellation or an output-handling failure, Annolid terminates and waits for the process, escalating to a forced shutdown if it does not exit within five seconds. On POSIX systems this signals the process group; on Windows forced shutdown targets the main process. Training logs retain a bounded tail for failure diagnostics. Numeric GPU index 0 is preserved when supplied through the shared command builders.

When exporting YOLO inference to LabelMe, detection-only results are saved as rectangles with class labels, confidence scores, and instance IDs. This applies to both streamed inference and selected video frame ranges. Segmentation results retain polygon export; pose results retain keypoints and the existing optional bounding-box behavior. The pose bounding-box option does not suppress rectangles from detection-only models.

docs.title: Codex and ACP
docs.text:
Annolid now supports Codex in more than one way. The easiest mental model is:

  • openai_codex: Codex as a cloud model, authenticated through ChatGPT/Codex OAuth-style credentials.
  • codex_cli: Codex as a local CLI runtime for conservative text-first execution.
  • ACP: a long-lived external coding session that Annolid can keep open across turns.

These modes solve different problems. You do not need all of them at once.

docs.title: Which Mode Should I Use?
docs.text:
Use openai_codex when:

  • you want Codex to be the main model in Annolid Bot,
  • you want normal model-style chat behavior,
  • you want the best default behavior for cloud Codex access.

Use codex_cli when:

  • you already have the codex CLI installed locally,
  • you want a simple local fallback,
  • you want session continuity through the Codex CLI thread system.

Use ACP when:

  • you want Annolid to keep a coding session alive across multiple prompts,
  • you want an IDE or external client to talk to Annolid over stdio,
  • you want to route follow-up coding instructions into the same long-lived session instead of starting over each turn.

docs.title: 1. openai_codex Cloud Provider
docs.text:
This is the main Codex provider inside Annolid.

Current behavior:

  • default model: openai-codex/gpt-5.4
  • default transport: auto
  • auto means WebSocket-first with SSE fallback
  • explicit transport values supported: auto, websocket, sse

Annolid keeps the provider separate from regular openai configuration because the auth and transport behavior are different.

Practical note:

  • Annolid auto-detects local Codex OAuth credentials in the runtime. You do not need to paste an API key into the Annolid UI for openai_codex.
  • In AI Model Settings, use Refresh to check the local Codex login state immediately, or click Save and Annolid will detect and store non-secret auth status metadata automatically.
  • If the required Python packages are missing, Annolid will return a direct setup error instead of a vague provider failure.

Required packages for this mode:

  • oauth_cli_kit
  • httpx
  • websockets

Example install inside the project environment:

source .venv/bin/activate
pip install oauth-cli-kit httpx websockets

docs.title: 2. codex_cli Local Provider
docs.text:
This mode uses the local codex executable instead of Annolid’s cloud provider stack.

Current behavior:

  • default model: codex-cli/gpt-5.3-codex
  • text-first runtime
  • default sandbox: read-only
  • optional coding sandbox: workspace-write
  • Codex CLI thread IDs are persisted so later turns can resume the same Codex thread
  • GUI chat sessions pass the Annolid session ID through to preserve continuity

This mode is useful when the local Codex CLI is already installed and you want a simpler runtime path. Use the default read-only sandbox for review, explanation, and planning tasks. Use workspace-write only when the user explicitly wants Codex to make code changes in the selected workspace.

Requirements:

  • codex must be available on PATH

Check it with:

codex --help

docs.title: Transport Behavior for openai_codex
docs.text:
Annolid’s openai_codex provider now supports the same transport model users expect from OpenClaw-style Codex integration:

  • websocket: force websocket transport
  • sse: force SSE transport
  • auto: try websocket first, then fall back to SSE automatically

Why this matters:

  • websocket is the preferred fast path,
  • SSE is the compatibility path,
  • auto gives the best default for most users.

Advanced users can set this in ~/.annolid/llm_settings.json:

{
  "provider": "openai_codex",
  "openai_codex": {
    "base_url": "https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses",
    "transport": "auto",
    "preferred_models": ["openai-codex/gpt-5.4"]
  }
}

If the websocket attempt fails in auto mode, Annolid falls back to SSE automatically.

docs.title: Long-Lived ACP Sessions
docs.text:
ACP stands for Agent Client Protocol. In Annolid, ACP is the session-oriented runtime for external coding harness workflows.

What that means in practice:

  • Annolid can create a coding session once,
  • keep it open across prompts,
  • queue follow-up requests into the same session,
  • cancel the active turn without destroying the whole session,
  • run in either read-only or workspace-write Codex CLI sandbox mode,
  • expose the session over stdio for IDE integrations.

This is different from one-shot provider chat. ACP is for ongoing coding work.

docs.title: What Annolid Stores for ACP Sessions
docs.text:
Annolid keeps ACP session state under the local session store in:

  • ~/.annolid/sessions/

Annolid also tracks Codex CLI thread continuity for ACP-backed Codex CLI runs, so follow-up prompts can resume the same Codex context instead of starting a fresh local thread each time.

docs.title: Cancel Behavior
docs.text:
ACP cancel, and the Annolid Bot coding_session_abort tool, do not tear down the whole session.

Current behavior:

  • the active turn is aborted,
  • the session stays alive,
  • the next prompt can reuse the same ACP session.

This makes ACP suitable for IDE workflows where the user may stop a long turn and immediately retry with a narrower instruction.

docs.title: Stdio ACP Bridge for IDEs
docs.text:
Annolid now exposes a formal stdio ACP bridge.

Run it with:

annolid-run agent acp bridge --workspace /path/to/repo

This starts a stdio server that external tools can spawn and communicate with.

Current ACP-native methods supported:

  • initialize
  • newSession
  • loadSession
  • prompt
  • cancel
  • listSessions
  • health
  • shutdown

Annolid also accepts compatibility aliases used by OpenClaw-style clients, including:

  • sessions_spawn
  • sessions_send
  • sessions_poll
  • sessions_list
  • sessions_close

docs.title: What the Bridge Does
docs.text:
The stdio bridge:

  • maps external ACP client sessions to Annolid ACP runtime sessions,
  • keeps session IDs stable for the life of the bridge process,
  • emits session update notifications,
  • supports long-lived coding workflows over stdio.

Annolid also bounds idle ACP client sessions so a long-running IDE process does not grow an unbounded in-memory session map.

ACP session workspaces are bounded by the bridge workspace. Client cwd and sessions.spawn.workspace values may be the bridge root or a subdirectory under it; paths outside that root are rejected. Launch the bridge at the repository or parent workspace that should be available to the external client.

docs.title: Example IDE Launch Pattern
docs.text:
If your editor supports custom stdio agent servers, the command usually looks like:

annolid-run agent acp bridge --workspace /absolute/path/to/repo

The editor then sends ACP messages over stdin/stdout.

docs.title: Cloud Codex as Main Model
docs.text:
Use this if you want Annolid Bot itself to talk directly to Codex:

  1. Ensure Codex OAuth-style credentials are available to Annolid.
  2. Install required packages in .venv.
  3. Set provider to openai_codex. Do not enter an API key in the UI for this provider.
  4. Leave transport on auto unless you are debugging transport issues.

docs.title: Local Codex CLI Fallback
docs.text:
Use this if you prefer the local CLI path:

  1. Install the codex CLI.
  2. Set provider to codex_cli.
  3. Keep using the same Annolid chat session to preserve Codex CLI thread continuity.
  4. For implementation tasks, start a coding session with sandbox set to workspace-write; for review and explanation, keep read-only.

docs.title: IDE or Thread-Oriented Coding Work
docs.text:
Use this if you want persistent coding sessions:

  1. Launch annolid-run agent acp bridge --workspace /path/to/repo.
  2. Connect your IDE or ACP-compatible client over stdio.
  3. Reuse the returned ACP session ID for follow-up prompts.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
If openai_codex fails immediately:

  • verify oauth_cli_kit, httpx, and websockets are installed in .venv
  • check that the Codex OAuth/token source is available to the current runtime

If codex_cli fails immediately:

  • verify codex is installed and on PATH
  • run codex --help manually

If websocket transport is unstable:

  • leave transport set to auto so Annolid can fall back to SSE
  • force sse only if you want to disable websocket attempts entirely

If an ACP session seems stuck:

  • send cancel
  • reuse the same session with a narrower prompt
  • restart the bridge if the external client and bridge state are out of sync

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Annolid’s Codex support is now split into clear layers:

  • openai_codex for cloud Codex with transport-aware runtime selection
  • codex_cli for local Codex CLI execution with thread continuity
  • ACP for long-lived external coding sessions
  • stdio ACP bridge for IDE and tool integration

That separation makes Codex behavior easier to understand, easier to debug, and safer to extend.

docs.title: CoWTracker Point Tracking
docs.text: CoWTracker is an optional point-tracking backend for videos where you want Annolid to propagate labeled points through a recording. It uses the same reviewable Annolid point-tracking contract as CoTracker and TAPNext: manually saved point prompts, optional polygon-derived grid points, and LabelMe-compatible JSON outputs.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
For a workstation that needs the GUI, common tracking runtime, and CoWTracker-specific dependency, install Annolid with these extras:

pip install "annolid[gui,tracking,cowtracker]"

If you are working from a local checkout:

source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e ".[gui,tracking,cowtracker]"

If Annolid is already installed in an environment that has the tracking runtime, you can add only the CoWTracker dependency:

pip install "safetensors>=0.4.0"

The first run needs an internet connection so Annolid can fetch the CoWTracker checkpoint from Hugging Face.

docs.title: GUI Workflow
docs.text:
1. Open a video in Annolid.
  2. Go to a frame where the target landmarks are visible.
  3. Add manual point labels for the landmarks you want to track.
  4. Optionally add a polygon around a region if you want Annolid to sample multiple tracking points inside it.
  5. Save the annotation for that frame.
  6. Select CoWTracker from the model dropdown.
  7. Start tracking from the current frame.
  8. Review the predicted frame JSON files and correct drift before using the data for analysis.

For long videos, validate a short representative range first. CoWTracker uses a windowed offline tracker, so first-run latency includes dependency import, checkpoint download if needed, model initialization, and the first tracking window.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
CoWTracker writes LabelMe-compatible JSON files into the video result folder, the same folder Annolid uses for other tracking outputs:

<video_name>/<video_name>_000000001.json
<video_name>/<video_name>_000000002.json
...

Each predicted shape is saved as a point with the original label, tracked coordinate, visibility flag, and backend description. These files remain reviewable in the GUI and can be exported through the usual Annolid workflows.

docs.title: VGGT Runtime Notes
docs.text:
CoWTracker uses a minimal vendored VGGT runtime subset under:

annolid/tracker/cowtracker/cowtracker/thirdparty/vggt

At runtime, Annolid resolves VGGT in this order:

  1. use the vendored subset when it is present and complete;
  2. fall back to an externally installed vggt package.

If neither runtime is available, CoWTracker raises a dependency error with install hints. Maintainer-facing vendoring details, required file lists, and packaging checks live in annolid/tracker/cowtracker/README.md.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem What to check CoWTracker is missing from the model choices Confirm the active environment includes the tracking runtime and CoWTracker dependency. First run appears slow Confirm the checkpoint is downloading from Hugging Face and that the environment has enough disk space. Dependency error mentions safetensors Install pip install "annolid[gui,tracking,cowtracker]" or pip install "safetensors>=0.4.0" in the active environment. Dependency error mentions VGGT Confirm the vendored VGGT subset is present, or install an external vggt package compatible with the CoWTracker runtime. No point prompts found Save at least one manual point or polygon annotation before tracking. Tracking results are poor Use clearer seed points, start from a sharper frame, or correct and restart from the first drift frame.

docs.title: When to Use a Different Tracker
docs.text:
Use CoWTracker when you need an alternative point tracker and want outputs as reviewable tracked points.

Use TAPNext for ONNX-only point tracking, or use a segmentation tracker such as Cutie or SAM3 when you need full masks or polygons.

docs.title: Deployment & Docs Authoring Workflow
docs.text: Annolid publishes multiple documentation surfaces from this repository and ships a local workflow so contributors can edit website/ and docs/ side-by-side with live reload, strict link/asset validation, and reproducible showcase generation.

docs.title: Source-of-Truth Layout
docs.text:
• website/: landing page (index.html) and landing assets (website/assets/ → published as /website-assets/)
  • docs/: canonical MkDocs Material source for /portal/ and mirrored root compatibility routes
  • docs/imgs/showcase/: generated screenshots, animated tracking demos, and offline 3D simulation captures
  • docs/assets/reports/: self-contained interactive example artifacts (such as mouse083_report.html)
  • docs/tutorials/: worked walkthroughs, focused markdown guides, and Jupyter notebooks
  • scripts/site_workflow.py: unified local staging, live preview/watch server, and strict site validator
  • scripts/generate_docs_showcase.py: reproducible generator for video/tracking showcase visuals, simulation screenshots, and live HTML5 reports

docs.title: 1. Preview Website + Docs Portal Together
docs.text:
Because website/index.html references /website-assets/... and /portal/... (matching production annolid.com), use the combined staging preview instead of opening website/index.html directly from disk:

# Stage combined landing page + /portal/ into .site_preview/ and serve at http://127.0.0.1:8080/
make site-preview

# Same preview with automatic live rebuild when website/, docs/, or mkdocs.yml changes
make site-watch

You can also invoke the underlying Python tool directly with custom options:

.venv/bin/python scripts/site_workflow.py preview --watch --port 8080 --open
  • Editing website/ syncs instantaneously without waiting for MkDocs.
  • Editing docs/ or mkdocs.yml triggers an automatic MkDocs rebuild and re-stage.
  • .site_preview/ is gitignored so local preview artifacts never pollute commits.

docs.title: 2. Validate Before Committing
docs.text:
Run one command to validate both website/ and docs/ locally:

make site-check

scripts/site_workflow.py check verifies:

  1. required source files exist (website/index.html, docs/index.md, mkdocs.yml, docs/requirements_mkdocs.txt),
  2. the production CI title contract in website/index.html (Annolid | Research-Grade Animal Behavior AI) is preserved,
  3. every website-assets/... reference resolves in website/assets/,
  4. every /portal/... link in website/index.html resolves inside the built MkDocs output,
  5. every local image reference across published Markdown docs exists on disk,
  6. mkdocs build --strict --clean succeeds with zero warnings/errors,
  7. no machine-local absolute paths leaked into docs/, website/, or generated HTML examples, and
  8. showcase and website assets stay within size budgets (below the pre-commit 6 MB limit).

docs.title: 3. Regenerate Showcase Screenshots, Animations & Simulation Captures
docs.text:
Regenerate offline 3D simulation screenshots (Two-Mouse, 13-Keypoint Pose, Fly-Brain LIF Connectome, FlyBody 3D) and sync them into website/assets/images/showcase/:

make showcase-sims

Regenerate video tracking visuals, animated tracking GIF, behavior storyboard, ethogram/kinematics dashboard, zone analysis chart, offscreen GUI screenshot, and sanitized live HTML5 report from any Annolid-tracked video:

make showcase-video VIDEO=/path/to/your_tracked_video.mp4

Both targets wrap scripts/generate_docs_showcase.py, which automatically syncs shared showcase assets from docs/imgs/showcase/ into website/assets/images/showcase/ so the website and docs portal stay visually aligned.

docs.title: Published Targets
docs.text:
• /: landing page from website/ (website/assets/ mounted at /website-assets/)
  • /portal/: canonical MkDocs Material documentation portal
  • root docs routes such as /installation/, /workflows/, and /reference/ for backward compatibility
  • /book/: notebook-oriented Jupyter Book surface published separately

docs.title: GitHub Actions Pipelines
docs.text:
• docs-quality.yml: builds MkDocs in strict mode and runs markdownlint across primary docs pages.
  • docs-pages.yml: builds MkDocs and uploads the HTML artifact for review/validation.
  • healthonrails-site-sync.yml: syncs landing page, /portal/, root compatibility routes, legacy redirects, and /book/ to healthonrails/healthonrails.github.io on main.
  • book-pages.yml: builds the Jupyter Book surface.
  • CI.yml: runs repository-wide tests and validation checks.

docs.title: Deployment Principles
docs.text:
• Keep docs/ as the canonical user-facing documentation source.
  • Always run make site-check (or mkdocs build --strict --clean --config-file mkdocs.yml) before merging.
  • Keep publication reproducible and debuggable with ephemeral local staging (.site_preview/).
  • Preserve compatibility routes and legacy redirect stubs (scripts/write_legacy_redirects.sh).
  • Never commit machine-local absolute paths into docs, HTML examples, or scripts.

docs.title: DINOv3 Keypoint Tracking
docs.text:
DINOv3 Keypoint Tracker propagates manually labeled body-part points through a video without training a pose-estimation model for the target dataset. It uses frozen DINO-family patch descriptors for appearance matching, a local motion-prior search, optional mask constraints, stateful track memory, and Lucas-Kanade pixel refinement for sub-patch motion.

This backend is a sparse-label accelerator. It is useful when you need reviewable keypoint trajectories from a few manual seed frames. It is not a new DINO model, and it is not a replacement for supervised pose estimation when you need a reusable model trained across many videos, camera setups, or animals.

For an end-to-end worked example combining whole-animal instance polygons with 14 anatomical keypoints (nose, left_ear, right_ear, neck, left_hip, right_hip, tail_base per mouse), see the Resident-Intruder Walkthrough (mouse083_task1_annotator1).

docs.title: When To Use It
docs.text:
Use DINOv3 Keypoint Tracker when:

  • you have a video-specific tracking job and want to avoid dense manual keypoint labeling;
  • the same landmarks are visible across nearby frames;
  • you can review and correct occasional drift;
  • masks or polygons are available, or the local appearance around each keypoint is distinctive enough to track without masks.

Use a pose-estimation workflow instead when:

  • you need a reusable model for many unseen videos;
  • the animal undergoes large viewpoint changes not represented by the seed frames;
  • you need high-throughput inference after a labeled training set is already available;
  • you need benchmarked pose-model outputs rather than per-video reviewed propagation.

docs.title: What It Tracks
docs.text:
The tracker starts from saved LabelMe-compatible Annolid annotations:

  • point shapes become named keypoints to track;
  • polygon or mask shapes are optional but recommended because they constrain ambiguous points to the instance;
  • a plain point without instance metadata is associated via matching group_id first and otherwise with the single polygon that contains it, while explicit instance_label metadata always wins;
  • occluded keypoint visibility (kp_visibility / kp_visible) is preserved across reads and writes;
  • later manually corrected frames act as new seed anchors, and restarting tracking after an already-tracked segment automatically resumes state from the latest persisted frame while keeping manual appearance anchors.

For multi-animal videos, avoid repeated plain point labels such as nose with no instance or group_id context. Annolid disambiguates same-class polygons with distinct group_id values (for example two mouse polygons with group_id 0 and 1) while preserving their saved polygon labels and group_ids across round-trips, alongside instance_label and display_label flags. Same-named points with distinct instance or group_id metadata remain separate when saving predictions or rerunning tracking. In scripted LabelMe JSON, set group_id or instance_label/display_label explicitly for each point; in the GUI, check the saved frame before a long run to confirm the point belongs to the intended animal. In the GUI, placing a point inside overlapping polygons automatically binds it to the selected polygon, the only containing polygon still missing that landmark, or the polygon chosen in the owner prompt. When plain points fall inside overlapping or concentric polygons on disk, Annolid resolves ownership deterministically via instance prefixes, landmark uniqueness, anchored pose clusters / non-overlapping mask cores, temporal continuity from prior or neighboring frames, and nested concentric scale / interior-depth geometry when one polygon is strictly nested inside a larger one. If a single isolated frame still has identical or nearly equal overlapping polygons with no instance or temporal cue, the GUI offers to jump directly to that frame before starting tracking, annolid-run track-qc <result_dir> --strict flags ambiguous_keypoint_ownership (exit code 2), and programmatic callers can configure CutieDinoTrackerConfig(ambiguous_point_policy=...) ("withhold" by default, "error" to raise AmbiguousKeypointError immediately, or "polygon_order" for deterministic declaration-order tie-breaking on legacy exports).

Keep display labels stable across frames and animals. Labels such as nose, leftear, rightear, tail_base, fore_top, or abdomen_bot should mean the same anatomical point every time.

docs.title: How The Backend Works
docs.text:
The implementation separates the feature backbone from the tracker logic:

  • annolid/features/dino_models.py defines the supported DINOv3, DINOv2, Google EmbeddingGemma 2, Google SigLIP 2, on-device MobileNetV4 / MobileNetV3, and RADIO-compatible feature backbones.
  • annolid/features/dinov3_extractor.py and annolid/features/google_vision_extractor.py load the selected Hugging Face, timm, or torchvision backbone, select CPU, CUDA, or MPS, snap image sizes to patch/stride multiples, handle modality-selective loading (including direct safetensors vision-tower loading when a cached checkpoint's nested vision_config.model_type is registered in transformers), project multimodal vision tokens into the aligned embedding space before Matryoshka channel truncation (embedding_matryoshka_dim), and return normalized dense patch grids (plus optional Gaussian-vignetted crop embeddings via embed_keypoint_regions).
  • annolid/tracking/gaussian_region.py, annolid/tracking/dino_keypoint_types.py, annolid/tracking/overlap_assignment.py, and annolid/tracking/video_seed_utils.py define mask-aware Gaussian region descriptors, sub-patch continuous Gaussian sampling, drift-free rotation-tolerant Gaussian pixel-region ZNCC template banks with 2D Hessian sub-pixel refinement, tracker state structures, overlapping-polygon point disambiguation, and shared seed/resume frame orchestration across keypoint processors.
  • annolid/tracking/dino_keypoint_tracker.py turns those patch grids into stateful point tracks.

Each manual point initializes a track with its current descriptor, reference descriptor, manual-anchor codebook, optional Gaussian-weighted pixel/gradient template, appearance codebook, support probes, velocity, quality state, and optional structural or symmetry state. On each new frame, Annolid:

  1. extracts the current dense feature grid;
  2. optionally debiases coordinate-correlated feature responses and builds mask-aware Gaussian regional descriptors around each instance so contour landmarks (nose, ears, paws, tail) integrate foreground neighborhood context without background bleed;
  3. estimates the current point from batched per-point pyramidal Lucas-Kanade flow, lazily computing dense Farneback flow only if per-point LK is unavailable, and falling back to previous velocity when neither flow observation is valid;
  4. searches a bounded candidate region around the motion prior;
  5. scores candidates with vectorized feature similarity, appearance/context/support evidence, mask or structure priors, backward consistency, and a motion penalty;
  6. resolves one-to-one assignments so two tracks do not claim the same best candidate;
  7. refines sub-patch coordinates with connected similarity peaks, Lucas-Kanade optical flow, and optional drift-free Gaussian-weighted pixel/gradient ZNCC template matching anchored to the manual seed;
  8. updates descriptors (optionally sampled continuously at sub-patch coordinates), velocity, quality, support probes, and output annotation metadata.

This split matters in practice: DINO descriptors provide robust coarse appearance correspondence, while optical flow handles small movements inside a 16-pixel ViT patch.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Install Annolid with GUI, model, and tracking dependencies:

pip install "annolid[gui,ml,tracking]"

For a local checkout, use the repository environment:

source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e ".[gui,ml,tracking]"

The one-line installer default gui profile also installs the model and tracking extras used by this workflow. The first DINOv3 run may need Hugging Face access. For gated DINOv3 checkpoints, accept the model license on Hugging Face and authenticate once:

hf auth login

You can also set HF_TOKEN in the active environment. To use a shared local Hugging Face cache:

export DINOV3_LOCATION=/path/to/hf-cache

The optional RADIO backbone requires open-clip-torch; choose a DINOv2 or DINOv3 backbone if that package is not installed.

docs.title: Choose A Feature Backbone
docs.text:
Open Tools -> Advanced Parameters -> Tracker -> DINO feature model and pick a model. The default is the small DINOv3 ViT-S/16 checkpoint because it is the best starting point for interactive tracking.

Common choices:

Model Best use facebook/dinov3-vits16-pretrain-lvd1689m Default interactive tracking; fastest DINOv3 option. facebook/dinov3-vits16plus-pretrain-lvd1689m Slightly stronger small DINOv3 descriptors. facebook/dinov3-vitb16-pretrain-lvd1426 Medium offline runs when ViT-S is not distinctive enough. facebook/dinov3-vitl16-pretrain-lvd1689m Higher-memory offline runs. google/embeddinggemma-2 Open lightweight 170M vision tower (768d with 512/256/128 Matryoshka dims; selective tower loading in bfloat16/float32; requires transformers>=5.19). google/siglip2-base-patch16-224 or google/siglip2-so400m-patch16-384 Open dense ViT/16 vision encoders with dynamic position interpolation. timm/mobilenetv4_conv_small.e2400_r224_in1k or torchvision/mobilenet_v3_small Fast on-device stride-8 multi-scale CNN pyramids (2x finer spatial grid than 16px ViTs) for low-latency CPU/MPS runs. facebook/dinov2-base or facebook/dinov2-large Open fallback when DINOv3 access is unavailable. nvidia/C-RADIOv4-SO400M Compatible feature backbone for specialized workflows.

List the supported catalog from the active environment:

annolid-run dinov3-models --list

Pre-download or verify a model before opening the GUI:

annolid-run dinov3-models --model facebook/dinov3-vits16-pretrain-lvd1689m
annolid-run dinov3-models --local-files-only --model facebook/dinov3-vits16-pretrain-lvd1689m

docs.title: GUI Workflow
docs.text:
1. Open a video in Annolid.
  2. Navigate to a frame where the landmarks are visible and sharp.
  3. Add point labels for the keypoints you want to track.
  4. For multi-animal videos, verify that each point has the intended instance association before starting a long run.
  5. Add polygons or masks for the animal instances when available.
  6. Save the annotation for that frame.
  7. Open Tools -> Advanced Parameters -> Tracker.
  8. Choose DINO feature model and, if useful, a Tracker preset.
  9. Select DINOv3 Keypoint Tracker from the model dropdown.
  10. Click the prediction button to track from the current frame.
  11. Review the generated JSON files, correct drift, save the corrected frame, and rerun from that frame when needed.

For long videos, validate a short difficult segment first. Confirm that the tracked points survive crossings, occlusions, and fast motion before processing the full recording.

docs.title: Presets And Important Parameters
docs.text:
The tracker exposes presets through Tools -> Advanced Parameters -> Tracker:

Preset Use fly_70fps_keypoints Small, fast motions such as high-frame-rate fly keypoints. Uses tight search, positional debiasing, backward consistency, coherent peak refinement, support probes, context descriptors, and a small Lucas-Kanade window. rodent_30fps_occlusions Larger animal motion and occlusions. Uses wider search, stronger mask/structure support, larger appearance bundles, more support probes, and a larger Lucas-Kanade window.

Key settings:

  • DINO feature model and Embedding Matryoshka dim: select the frozen feature backbone and optional prefix truncation (768, 512, 256, 128) for Matryoshka-trained models such as google/embeddinggemma-2 (the dialog displays live runtime readiness via check_dino_model_runtime_support). When switching to a non-Matryoshka backbone (DINOv3, SigLIP 2, MobileNet), embedding_matryoshka_strict_mrl=True (default) safely keeps the full descriptor channels; programmatic callers that explicitly set embedding_matryoshka_strict_mrl=False get deterministic row-orthonormal compression so all channels and multi-scale CNN stages remain represented.
  • Gaussian region radius / sigma and Sub-patch continuous Gaussian sampling: aggregate a mask-aware Gaussian patch neighborhood (region_descriptor_radius, region_descriptor_sigma, region_descriptor_blend, region_descriptor_mask_aware) and sample descriptors at continuous sub-patch coordinates (region_subpatch_sampling) instead of snapping to integer patch cells.
  • Drift-free Gaussian pixel template refinement: anchors a zero-mean, unit-weighted-norm multi-orientation Gaussian intensity + signed-Sobel ZNCC template bank around manual seed points (pixel_region_refine_enabled, pixel_region_window, pixel_region_sigma, pixel_region_search_radius_px, pixel_region_weight, pixel_region_num_orientations=12) guided by 2D Procrustes constellation rotation and 2D Hessian sub-pixel peak fitting so small frame-to-frame optical-flow errors do not accumulate even across large in-plane animal turns.
  • Clamp keypoints to instance mask and Mask snap radius: keep points inside the selected instance when masks are available. Patch masks are quantized via area occupancy (cv2.INTER_AREA) so thin appendages (tail_mid, tail_tip, paws) remain represented on the ViT grid, cross-instance foreground masks exclude candidates that land strictly inside another animal during close huddling, and sudden partial mask truncation falls back safely without dropping well-supported skeletal points.
  • Occluded seed keypoint handling: seed points marked occluded (kp_visibility = 1 / kp_visible = false) do not pollute manual anchor codebooks or pixel templates with the occluding surface; they inherit clean descriptors from visible homologous landmarks when available, follow 2D Procrustes constellation motion while occluded without stealing active sibling patches, and re-acquire visible = true only when emerging at a distinct, well-supported anatomical position.
  • Elongated ROI token cap and accelerator memory resilience: Dinov3Config(max_long_side=1408) preserves full short_side=768 resolution on standard 4:3 and 16:9 frames while bounding ViT token count on wide multi-animal band crops; both Dinov3FeatureExtractor and CutieMaskManager automatically flush accelerator memory and migrate to CPU if CUDA/MPS runs out of memory mid-video.
  • Search tighten, Velocity gain, Flow gain, and Min/Max radius: control the local motion-prior search.
  • DINOv3 positional debias: suppresses coordinate-correlated feature responses that can pin points to image locations.
  • DINOv3 backward consistency: prefers candidates that map back to the previous feature location.
  • Coherent peak refinement: refines around the connected similarity peak instead of unrelated nearby peaks.
  • Pixel refinement: the tracker presets configure Lucas-Kanade sub-patch correction; programmatic callers can tune its blend weight, window size, error threshold, and max jump through the pixel_refine_* runtime fields.
  • Symmetry pairing: active PoseSchema symmetry pairs (including inferred left/right landmark pairs such as left_forepaw / right_forepaw) are automatically registered per animal instance to discourage left/right swaps.
  • Multi-animal assignment and kinematic constraints: programmatic callers can enable tracking_enable=True to activate Hungarian global candidate assignment (tracking_matcher_algorithm="hungarian"), per-frame velocity gating (tracking_constraint_max_velocity_px), skeletal limb-stretch bounds (tracking_enforce_skeletal_constraints, tracking_constraint_limb_std_multiplier), instance centroid/pose/size penalties, and occlusion template reset (tracking_instance_dropout_timeout_frames).
  • Trajectory post-smoothing: programmatic callers can enable optional confidence-gated one_euro, ema, or innovation-gated kalman post-smoothing via tracking_smoother_enable, tracking_smoother_mode, and the tracking_smoother_* runtime fields.
  • Ambiguous point policy: programmatic callers can set ambiguous_point_policy on CutieDinoTrackerConfig ("withhold" default, "error" fail-fast AmbiguousKeypointError, or "polygon_order" declaration-order tie-breaking).

docs.title: Outputs And Review Contract
docs.text:
DINOv3 Keypoint Tracker writes LabelMe-compatible JSON files into the standard Annolid result folder:

<video_name>/<video_name>_000000001.json
<video_name>/<video_name>_000000002.json
...

Predicted point shapes keep their labels and include tracking metadata such as backend description, quality, velocity, miss count, display label, and instance label. The tracker itself does not write a summary CSV; export or summarize the reviewed JSON files through the usual Annolid analysis tools after corrections are complete.

The recommended correction loop is:

  1. run tracking from a clean seed frame;
  2. inspect the first frame where a keypoint drifts or swaps;
  3. correct the point manually and save that frame;
  4. rerun tracking from the corrected frame;
  5. keep corrections as sparse reseed frames rather than relabeling every frame.

At a correction frame, a saved manual polygon takes precedence over the previous tracked mask. When the correction contains only points, the previous mask is reused for that instance when available.

docs.title: Choosing Among Point And Mask Backends
docs.text: Backend Use it when DINOv3 Keypoint Tracker You want sparse, named keypoint propagation with reviewable LabelMe outputs and optional masks. TAPNext (ONNX) You want an ONNX point tracker with fixed model assets and no DINO/Hugging Face feature backbone. See TAPNext ONNX Point Tracking. CoTracker You want joint point tracking through a chunk using the official CoTracker model. CoWTracker You want an alternative dense/windowed point tracker and can install the optional runtime. See CoWTracker Point Tracking. YOLO pose or DinoKPSEG You want a trainable pose/keypoint model for repeated inference on future videos. INSID3 Video You want DINOv3 in-context segmentation masks, not direct point tracking. Masks from segmentation workflows can still help constrain keypoints. Cutie or SAM3 You need masks or polygons rather than point trajectories. See SAM3 for SAM3 tracking and correction.

docs.title: Programmatic Use
docs.text:
from annolid.tracking.configuration import CutieDinoTrackerConfig
from annolid.tracking.dino_keypoint_tracker import DinoKeypointVideoProcessor

runtime = CutieDinoTrackerConfig.from_preset(
    "rodent_30fps_occlusions",
    patch_model_name="facebook/dinov3-vits16-pretrain-lvd1689m",
)

processor = DinoKeypointVideoProcessor(
    video_path="/path/to/video.mp4",
    result_folder=None,
    model_name="facebook/dinov3-vits16-pretrain-lvd1689m",
    short_side=768,
    device=None,
    runtime_config=runtime,
)
processor.process_video()

The processor reads the saved seed annotation from the video result folder, tracks forward, and writes per-frame JSON outputs.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem What to check No manual PNG+JSON seed pairs found Save a labeled seed frame in the video result folder before starting tracking. DINOv3 model download fails Accept the gated model license, run hf auth login, set HF_TOKEN, or choose an open DINOv2 fallback. RADIO model import fails Install open-clip-torch or switch back to a DINO-family feature model. Model dropdown uses the wrong DINO backbone Reopen Tools -> Advanced Parameters -> Tracker, confirm DINO feature model, and check the log for the resolved model id. Points snap to the same image location Enable DINOv3 positional debias and reduce search radius if motion is small. Small joints appear stuck inside one patch Keep pixel refinement enabled and use the fly preset or a smaller Lucas-Kanade window. Left/right landmarks swap Add masks when possible, keep labels consistent, add more anchor points, and configure symmetry pairs in scripted workflows. Tracking drifts after occlusion Correct the first bad frame, save it, and rerun from that correction frame. CPU runs are slow Use CUDA or MPS when available, reduce short_side, validate short segments first, and pre-download the model before long runs.

docs.title: Two-Mice 3D Simulation Dataset & Tracking Evaluation
docs.text:
To generate deterministic multi-scenario two-mouse .mp4 videos, 3D depth-buffered instance/body-part masks, LabelMe JSONs, COCO pose + tracking splits, and side-by-side ground-truth vs. tracked diagnostic videos:

source .venv/bin/activate
python scripts/generate_two_mice_keypoint_tracking_eval.py --tag eval

Outputs are written under output/two_mice_keypoint_tracking_eval/ (pass --generate-only to export the videos and ground-truth dataset without running model inference, or --skip-generate to re-benchmark against existing sequences).

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: Use this page as the fastest path from installation to a verified Annolid session. The goal is not to finish a full project in one pass; it is to prove that your environment opens videos, saves annotations, and can run the command-line tools you will need later.

docs.title: 20-Minute Path
docs.text:
1. Install Annolid with your preferred method from Installation.
  2. Confirm commands resolve:
  3. annolid --help
  4. annolid-run --help
  5. Launch the GUI with annolid.
  6. Open a short sample video.
  7. Label one or more instances on a representative frame.
  8. Run tracking/propagation and review identity consistency.
  9. Export results for downstream analysis.

If this flow works, your environment is ready for full projects. If it fails, keep the video short and resolve the installation or codec issue before scaling to long recordings.

docs.title: Quick Environment Check
docs.text:
Recommended development setup in this repository:

uv venv .venv --python 3.11
source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -e ".[gui]"

Validate:

annolid --help
annolid-run list-models

For a user install that does not need source editing, prefer the one-line installer or the pip install "annolid[gui]" path in Installation.

docs.title: First GUI Session Checklist
docs.text:
• Open a short video.
  • Pick a representative seed frame.
  • Add labels, polygons, boxes, keypoints, zones, or behavior flags as needed.
  • Track or propagate forward/backward from the seed frame.
  • Review overlap, occlusion, swaps, and high-motion sections early.
  • Save LabelMe-compatible JSON files and export any analysis CSVs you need.

See the Resident-Intruder End-to-End Walkthrough (mouse083_task1_annotator1) for a real worked example with live tracking results, or Workflows for detailed operating patterns.

docs.title: First CLI Session Checklist
docs.text:
annolid-run --help
annolid-run list-models
annolid-run help train
annolid-run help predict
annolid-run help train <model>
annolid-run help predict <model>

Use run-config templates under annolid/configs/runs/ for reproducible jobs.

For built-in models, the model help view now shows a grouped quick reference before the full option list.

If you want Annolid Bot to drive those commands for you, use the typed annolid_run path described in Annolid Agent and annolid-run.
