docs.title: What each extra is for (with example use cases)
docs.text: Extra Install this when you need... Example use case audio audio decoding/playback helpers You want waveform-derived behavior features, microphone recording, or sound playback without installing audio stacks in every lab workstation. ai_chat hosted OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic provider SDKs You use GPT/OpenRouter/Claude-style providers instead of only local/Ollama-compatible paths. ml general ML/model runtime dependencies You need PyTorch, Transformers, Hugging Face Hub, ONNX Runtime, Hydra/OmegaConf, and model tooling but do not want every optional workflow. tracking common tracking workstation dependencies You need PyTorch, ONNX Runtime, Cutie-style config dependencies, and YOLO matching helpers on a maintained workstation. training TensorBoard dashboards and projector views You train models from Annolid and want live training curves or embedding projector output. yolo Ultralytics YOLO/YOLOE workflows You train YOLO models, run YOLOE prompt inference, or export YOLO detections to LabelMe JSON. cutie Cutie video object segmentation tracking runtime You run Cutie tracking on minimal installs and want the required Python packages installed up front. Minimal/default installs can still auto-install missing Cutie packages on first use. realtime serial/ZMQ realtime hardware integrations You use Bpod, realtime streams, or ZMQ control paths. large_image TIFF/OME-TIFF metadata and optional region-streaming backends You want large TIFF, BigTIFF, OME-TIFF, or virtual-slide style viewing without forcing those native libraries into every install. Leave it out for the default GUI install. remote_video network/remote video decoding through ffpyplayer You receive frames from Annolid's remote video player path. Leave it out for normal local video files and Python 3.14+ default installs. sam3 the SAM3-related segmentation workflow/features in Annolid You want stronger promptable segmentation on difficult frames and plan to use SAM3 tools in the GUI/CLI pipeline. The installer also attempts the optional SAM-HQ dependency for this profile. image_editing diffusion-based image editing/generation dependencies You are preparing augmented training images (inpainting/background edits) as part of annotation or data curation. text_to_speech built-in narration/read-aloud features You want captions/notes read aloud during review, accessibility workflows, or hands-free labeling sessions. qwen3_embedding Qwen3-based embedding/multimodal utilities You plan to run embedding-powered retrieval/comparison flows that rely on the Qwen3 stack. annolid_bot bundled Annolid Bot integrations (WhatsApp + Google Drive/Calendar + MCP) You want background services/integrations without installing each Bot extra individually. bot Annolid Bot integrations plus memory dependencies You want provider SDKs, channel integrations, MCP, browser automation, and LanceDB-backed memory in one extra. memory vector database dependencies for fast Annolid Bot memory You want LanceDB-backed semantic memory rather than the lightweight lexical path. all full-feature workstation profile You are setting up a maintained lab machine where install size is less important than having every optional integration ready.

docs.title: Practical install suggestions
docs.text:
• Minimal install (fastest, lowest dependency footprint): use --profile minimal / -Profile minimal.
  • Most common research annotation and tracking setup: use the default installer profile.
  • Common training workstation: add yolo,training.
  • Hosted AI chat providers: add ai_chat.
  • Accessibility or narrated review: add text_to_speech.
  • Data augmentation/image synthesis workflows: add image_editing.
  • Remote network video decoding: add remote_video.
  • Realtime hardware/streaming workflows: add realtime.
  • Only install qwen3_embedding if you explicitly use those embedding features.
  • If you use Annolid Bot integrations, add annolid_bot.

Use comma-separated values with no spaces, for example:

--extras sam3,text_to_speech

docs.title: large_image runtime note
docs.text:
The large_image extra installs the Python bindings, but pyvips and openslide-python may still require native system runtimes on your machine. This extra is optional; Annolid's normal GUI workflows do not depend on it.

If those runtimes are not available, Annolid will still open the file and will fall back to tifffile when available, but navigation can be slower on very large TIFF files.

docs.title: remote_video runtime note
docs.text: The remote_video extra installs ffpyplayer. On Python 3.14 and 3.15, ffpyplayer may need to build from source and require native FFmpeg development headers such as libpostproc. The default installer leaves this extra out so core GUI and local video workflows can install cleanly on Python 3.14+.

docs.title: SAM-HQ runtime note
docs.text: The one-line installers no longer install SAM-HQ during the default GUI setup. SAM-HQ is attempted only when a SAM-related profile such as --extras sam3 / -Extras sam3 or all is selected. This keeps the default installer independent of an extra GitHub source install and makes locked-down lab workstations easier to bootstrap.

docs.title: Cutie runtime note
docs.text: The cutie extra installs the Python runtime packages used by Cutie tracking. The default gui profile installs this extra up front. If a minimal install tries to run Cutie tracking and one of those packages is missing, Annolid attempts to install the missing packages into the active environment before loading the tracker. Set ANNOLID_AUTO_INSTALL_CUTIE_DEPS=0 to disable that automatic repair and show the exact install command instead.

docs.title: Recommended patterns
docs.text:
• Stable workstation install: use default one-liner first, then rerun with flags only if needed.
  • Headless or CI environment: use --no-interactive (and --no-gpu if GPU drivers are unavailable).
  • Shared lab server: set explicit --install-dir and --venv-dir to avoid confusion.

docs.title: GPU and device suggestions
docs.text:
Use this as a practical hardware guide before choosing flags.

Device / Platform Recommendation Suggested installer choice NVIDIA GPU workstation (Linux/Windows) Best performance for training + large-batch inference. Keep CUDA drivers current. Use default installer (do not pass --no-gpu / -NoGpu). Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3) Good local inference performance via MPS; stable for many annotation/tracking tasks. Use default installer on macOS. CPU-only laptop/VM Works for annotation and light inference, but slower for heavy models. Use --no-gpu (Linux/macOS) or -NoGpu (Windows). Shared HPC/server node Prefer reproducibility and explicit paths/env control. Use --no-interactive, explicit --install-dir/--venv-dir, optionally --use-conda.

docs.title: ONNX Runtime CPU/GPU behavior
docs.text:
Annolid uses ONNX Runtime for several model paths. The one-line installers keep the provider choice explicit:

  • Linux and Windows with an NVIDIA driver reporting CUDA 12.x or newer: install onnxruntime-gpu from the CUDA 12 package feed and validate that CUDAExecutionProvider is available.
  • Linux and Windows with CUDA 13.x driver reports: use the same stable CUDA 12 ONNX Runtime GPU wheel because NVIDIA drivers are backward compatible with CUDA 12 runtimes.
  • Linux and Windows without a CUDA 12-compatible NVIDIA driver: install CPU onnxruntime for compatibility.
  • macOS: install onnxruntime; ONNX acceleration uses CoreMLExecutionProvider when the installed wheel and macOS runtime expose it. There is no CUDA ONNX Runtime wheel for macOS.
  • --no-gpu / -NoGpu: skip GPU detection and install CPU ONNX Runtime.

If a CUDA 12-compatible NVIDIA driver is detected but CUDAExecutionProvider is missing after installation, the installer exits with a repair command instead of silently accepting a CPU-only ONNX Runtime install.

Manual repair inside the installer-created environment:

uv pip install --upgrade --force-reinstall onnxruntime-gpu --extra-index-url https://aiinfra.pkgs.visualstudio.com/PublicPackages/_packaging/onnxruntime-cuda-12/pypi/simple/
python -c "import onnxruntime as ort; print(ort.get_available_providers())"

docs.title: Device-specific tips
docs.text:
• If you have an NVIDIA GPU, verify drivers and CUDA runtime before install (nvidia-smi should work).
  • If GPU install fails or is unstable, rerun in CPU mode first (--no-gpu / -NoGpu) to get a working baseline quickly.
  • For remote servers without display, combine --no-interactive and CPU mode unless GPU runtime is already validated.
  • On Apple Silicon, use native arm64 Python/environment tools for best compatibility and speed.

docs.title: Verify installation
docs.text:
After install:

annolid --help

Launch GUI:

annolid

If annolid is not found, activate the environment printed by the installer and retry.

docs.title: Security note
docs.text:
Piping scripts from the internet is convenient but trust-based. For stricter security:

  • download script first,
  • inspect it,
  • then run locally with explicit options.

docs.title: Desktop launch and repeat installs
docs.text: Successful venv installs create Launch Annolid and Update Annolid shortcuts in the install directory. Use the update shortcut to retain the original profile, extras, environment path, and CPU/GPU preference. Existing environments are reused; Git updates must fast-forward and tracked local edits must be committed or stashed. Non-interactive runs no longer launch the GUI at completion. See the desktop launch and upgrade guide for platform details, recovery, and source-update limitations.

docs.title: Packaging and Distribution
docs.text: This document defines Annolid's install tiers, optional runtime contract, frozen app artifact policy, and release validation expectations.

docs.title: Install Tiers
docs.text:
Annolid keeps core and desktop GUI installs small and fast to start, while installing large optional model/viewer stacks on demand (or upfront via named profiles).

Tier Command Contract Core pip install annolid Import-safe core package for non-GUI workflows and library use. Includes pycocotools so mask/RLE polygon paths are available by default. GUI pip install "annolid[gui]" Lean desktop annotation GUI (PySide6-Essentials). Embedded WebEngine/3D/PDF viewers and ML stacks install on demand when opened. WebEngine pip install "annolid[webengine]" PySide6-Addons for embedded PDF.js, Three.js 3D, and embedded web dashboards (ABI-matched to the installed PySide6-Essentials version). ONNX pip install "annolid[onnx]" ONNX Runtime for interactive SAM, TapNext, and VideoMT inference. ML pip install "annolid[ml]" General model runtime tier: PyTorch, TorchVision, Transformers, Hugging Face Hub, ONNX Runtime, Hydra/OmegaConf, COCO tooling, and shared model helpers. Tracking pip install "annolid[tracking]" Maintained tracking workstation tier with PyTorch, ONNX Runtime, Cutie-style config dependencies, YOLO matching helpers, and related image/model utilities. Training pip install "annolid[training]" Training dashboard support such as TensorBoard. Bot pip install "annolid[bot]" Annolid Bot providers, channel integrations, MCP/browser automation helpers, and memory dependencies. Full pip install "annolid[all]" Convenience tier for fully provisioned lab machines where install size is less important than breadth.

Feature-specific extras such as scientific, pdf, model_downloads, sleap, cutie, sam3, yolo, large_image, remote_video, audio, text_to_speech, image_editing, ai_chat, and realtime remain available for narrower installs.

docs.title: One-Line Installer Profiles
docs.text:
The macOS/Linux and Windows one-line installers expose stable profiles:

Profile Extras minimal gui only gui gui only (default; optional runtimes install on demand) tracking gui,ml,tracking,cutie workstation gui,ml,tracking,cutie,sam3,training,webengine,pdf full gui,all

The default profile is gui. PyTorch and ONNX Runtime are installed upfront only when an ML/ONNX extra or profile (tracking, workstation, full) is selected; SAM-HQ is attempted only when a SAM-related extra such as sam, sam3, segment_anything, or all is selected. This keeps default installs small, fast, and independent of multi-gigabyte model downloads until needed.

Each successful installer run writes annolid-install-report.json in the install directory. The report includes the selected profile, resolved extras, Python version, OS, architecture, package manager, GPU decision, ONNX Runtime providers, SAM-HQ status, offline/wheelhouse settings, and failed optional steps.

docs.title: Desktop Bundle Contract
docs.text:
The frozen desktop archives are intentionally lean Unix-style annotation bundles. Current release binaries are built for macOS and Linux only, and their baseline contract is opening media/annotations and drawing/editing polygons. They must not bundle ML frameworks, training stacks, model checkpoints, generated runs, or optional service clients, and Annolid never mutates the bundled application directory itself (Annolid.app / annolid/_internal stays strictly read-only so code signatures and system-wide installs remain intact).

When a user opens a model, tracking, embedded WebEngine viewer, or other optional workflow:

  • Editable / virtualenv installs: missing optional packages are installed on demand into the active Python environment (or from a local --wheelhouse / ANNOLID_WHEELHOUSE).
  • Frozen desktop bundles (headless default): unprompted headless calls fail fast with the missing imports and exact pip install command instead of mutating the bundle.
  • Frozen desktop bundles (isolated User Runtime): when invoked interactively from Settings → Runtime & Optional Packages… (or the on-demand GUI prompt, annolid-run runtime install --user-runtime, or ANNOLID_FROZEN_USER_RUNTIME=1), Annolid installs ABI-matched binary wheels into an isolated user-space directory (~/.annolid/runtime/py<major>.<minor>-<platform>-<arch>/site-packages, overridable via ANNOLID_USER_RUNTIME_DIR). User-space installs use uv, a matching host Python 3.<minor>, or Annolid's built-in zero-toolchain PEP 427 offline wheelhouse installer (verifying wheelhouse-manifest.json and .dist-info/RECORD SHA256 digests without requiring uv, pip, or internet access). Set ANNOLID_FROZEN_USER_RUNTIME=0 to disable user-space runtime extensions completely.

docs.title: Air-Gapped Offline Wheelhouse Bundles
docs.text:
To support air-gapped research workstations, Annolid can export and verify portable, SHA256-checksummed wheelhouse folders:

annolid-run runtime bundle tracking sam3 --out ./annolid-wheelhouse
annolid-run runtime verify-bundle ./annolid-wheelhouse
annolid-run runtime install tracking sam3 --wheelhouse ./annolid-wheelhouse --offline

When wheelhouse-manifest.json is present in a wheelhouse folder, Annolid verifies file sizes and SHA256 checksums before installing any wheel.

docs.title: Optional Runtime Behavior
docs.text:
Frozen apps and lean installs intentionally exclude heavy optional runtimes. Code that opens optional workflows should use the central capability checker in annolid.infrastructure.capabilities to report:

  • whether the runtime is available,
  • which imports are missing,
  • the exact install command,
  • and the documentation link.

Optional runtime repair is controlled by ANNOLID_AUTO_INSTALL_OPTIONAL_DEPS. Set ANNOLID_AUTO_INSTALL_OPTIONAL_DEPS=0 to make optional workflows fail fast with an install command instead of trying to install missing packages.

Cutie tracking keeps its narrower compatibility switch as well. If Cutie packages are missing and ANNOLID_AUTO_INSTALL_CUTIE_DEPS is not disabled, Annolid attempts to install the required packages into the active environment before loading the tracker. Set ANNOLID_AUTO_INSTALL_CUTIE_DEPS=0 to make the workflow fail fast with an install command instead.

docs.title: Artifact Policy
docs.text:
Source distributions, wheels, PyInstaller folders, and final release archives must not include local checkpoints, model weights, generated runs, or heavyweight optional runtimes. The shared guard is:

python scripts/check_distribution_artifacts.py dist/*
python scripts/check_distribution_artifacts.py --kind bundle dist

The same policy rejects forbidden model suffixes such as .pt, .pth, .onnx, .safetensors, .engine, .weights, and known generated/runtime folders such as checkpoints, weights, runs, torch, torchvision, transformers, onnxruntime, ultralytics, and bundled model paths.

docs.title: Desktop Release Status
docs.text:
Current GitHub release binaries are PyInstaller onedir archives:

  • macOS: Annolid-macOS.zip
  • Linux: Annolid-Linux.tar.gz

Each archive is uploaded with:

  • a .sha256 checksum file,
  • a release manifest JSON,
  • and artifact guard validation before upload.

Signing and native installer packaging are staged but not yet treated as complete:

  • macOS target: signed .app, notarized .dmg, with an explicit arm64/x86_64 or universal binary decision.
  • Windows target: source/venv installation remains supported, but frozen Windows desktop archives are not published by the current release workflow.
  • Linux target: AppImage first, then .deb/.rpm if demand justifies maintaining native packages.

Until signing identities and native packaging jobs are configured, release manifests mark CI-built desktop archives as unsigned-ci-build. On macOS, archives are created with ditto so .framework symlinks and ad-hoc signatures remain intact; if macOS Gatekeeper blocks a browser-downloaded Annolid.app, clear the quarantine attribute (xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine Annolid.app) or allow it under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway.

docs.title: Update and Uninstall
docs.text:
For pip/venv installs:

python -m pip install --upgrade "annolid[gui]"
python -m pip uninstall annolid

For one-line installer source checkouts, activate the printed environment and update from the install directory:

git pull --recurse-submodules
python -m pip install --upgrade -e ".[gui]"

To remove a one-line installer setup, delete the install directory after saving any user data stored inside it.

docs.title: Release Validation
docs.text:
Before publishing a release, run the smallest checks that cover the changed surface:

source .venv/bin/activate
pytest
python -m build
python -m twine check dist/*
python scripts/check_distribution_artifacts.py dist/*

For desktop archives, also run:

python scripts/check_distribution_artifacts.py --kind bundle dist

Release artifacts should include SHA256 checksums and a manifest JSON. If signing is not available for a given release, the release notes and manifest must say so explicitly.

docs.title: Pose Estimation Workflow (SLEAP & DeepLabCut Parity)
docs.text:
Annolid provides an end-to-end pose estimation workflow spanning visual-diversity frame extraction, rapid multi-animal keypoint labeling, model training, DeepLabCut/SLEAP-grade evaluation, offline trajectory filtering and gap interpolation, active-learning outlier refinement, calibrated pose kinematics, and labeled skeleton video export.

For bidirectional format conversion with DeepLabCut, Lightning Pose, SLEAP (.slp, .pkg.slp, .analysis.h5), SimBA, movement, and COCO Keypoints, see DeepLabCut, SLEAP & Pose Interoperability.

docs.title: 1. Define a Skeleton (PoseSchema)
docs.text:
Choose a built-in species preset in Project Wizard → Pose Schema or Settings → Pose & Keypoint Manager:

  • Rodents: Mouse (5 keypoints), Mouse CalMS21 / MARS (7 keypoints), Mouse (9 keypoints), Mouse (11 keypoints), Mouse MaBE2022 (12 keypoints), Rat (8 keypoints)
  • Insects & Fish: Fly (5 keypoints), Fly Full-Body (12 keypoints), Fish (5 keypoints), Zebrafish Spine (5 keypoints)
  • Human: Human COCO (17 keypoints)

Skeleton definitions store canonical keypoint ordering, anatomical edges, left/right symmetry_pairs, flip_idx, optional custom 2D preview layouts, and multi-animal instance prefixes in pose_schema.json / .yaml. In the Keypoint Sequencer dock, drag any node in the skeleton preview to arrange a custom 2D anatomical layout (optionally over a loaded Ref Image…), or click two nodes to toggle an edge.

docs.title: 2. Extract Diverse Training Frames (kmeans & uniform)
docs.text:
Instead of sampling only random or high-motion frames, use visual-diversity k-means clustering (equivalent to DeepLabCut's default algo='kmeans' and SLEAP's image-clustering suggestions) or uniform spacing:

  • GUI: Open Video Tools → Extract frames (Ctrl+Shift+E), select kmeans (recommended for pose diversity) or uniform, and set the frame count.
  • CLI:
# Visually diverse frames via deterministic k-means++ clustering
annolid-run extract-frames trial.mp4 --algo kmeans --num-frames 50 -o ./frames_kmeans

# Evenly spaced frames across a subclip
annolid-run extract-frames trial.mp4 --algo uniform --num-frames 40 \
  --start-seconds 10 --end-seconds 120 -o ./frames_uniform

docs.title: 3. Annotate & Proofread Keypoints in the GUI
docs.text:
• Keypoint Sequencer (Ctrl+Shift+K or View → Docks → Keypoint Sequencer):
  • Lock keypoints in your desired click order, then place points sequentially.
  • Use Skip (Absent) to advance past out-of-frame landmarks without placing a dummy point, and Prev KP to step backward.
  • Enable Auto-advance to next instance on wrap in multi-animal scenes to step automatically from mouse_1 to mouse_2 after completing a skeleton.
  • Visibility, Whole-Skeleton Selection & Rigid Transforms:
  • Shift+Click places an occluded keypoint (v=1, rendered with dashed bones and hollow circles).
  • Right-click any selected keypoint on the canvas (or in the Labels panel) to Select Whole Pose Instance (selects all keypoints of that animal so dragging moves the entire skeleton together), Rotate Pose Left/Right (±15°) / Scale Pose Up/Down (±10%) around the skeleton centroid, Toggle Keypoint Visibility, Mark Keypoint Visible, or Mark Keypoint Occluded (Ctrl+Alt+I / V / O).
  • Live Canvas Pose Controls:
  • Open Analysis → Pose Estimation Workbench… (Ctrl+Shift+P) to switch live canvas coloring between By Instance (Animal), By Bodypart (DLC), and By Confidence (Score), adjust the live Canvas p-cutoff threshold, and toggle Show keypoint labels on canvas.

docs.title: 4. Evaluate Pose Models (eval-pose)
docs.text:
Compare any ground-truth and predicted pose datasets across LabelMe directories, AnnotationStore sidecars, SLEAP .slp / .analysis.h5, DeepLabCut .csv / .h5 / training projects, COCO Keypoints JSON, or Annolid tracking CSVs.

Metrics computed with multi-animal Hungarian matching:

  • DeepLabCut metrics: Pixel RMSE and MAE across all keypoints and restricted to score >= pcutoff.
  • SLEAP localization metrics: Median (p50), p75, p90, p95, and max Euclidean error (px).
  • PCK: Fixed-pixel PCK (2, 4, 8, 16 px) and instance-scale-normalized PCK (5%, 10%, 20%).
  • COCO / SLEAP OKS: mean_oks, mAP (0.50:0.05:0.95), AP50, AP75, and AR for arbitrary animal keypoint counts.
  • Detection & Symmetry: Keypoint/instance precision, recall, F1, and multi-animal Left/Right symmetry swap rate.
  • Per-Keypoint & Worst-Frame Tables: Ranked highest-error frames with double-click canvas seeking in Pose Estimation Workbench → 1. Evaluate Pose.
annolid-run eval-pose ./gt_labelme ./pred_labelme \
  --pose-schema ./pose_schema.json \
  --pcutoff 0.6 \
  --output-dir ./pose_eval_report

Writes pose_eval_report.json, pose_eval_per_keypoint.csv, pose_eval_worst_frames.csv, and a self-contained pose_eval_report.html with inline SVG error charts and PCK CDF curves.

docs.title: 5. Active-Learning Outlier Refinement (extract-outliers)
docs.text:
Automatically mine the highest-risk frames from model predictions (combining low keypoint confidence, per-keypoint velocity jumps, anatomical bone stretch/collapse, and missing keypoints) spaced by --min-frame-gap:

annolid-run extract-outliers ./pred_labelme \
  --video trial.mp4 \
  --pose-schema ./pose_schema.json \
  --num-frames 20 \
  --min-frame-gap 15 \
  --min-confidence 0.6 \
  -o ./refinement_batch

Annolid extracts the matching PNG frames, writes pre-populated editable LabelMe JSONs (plus pose_schema.json and outlier_frames_manifest.json), and lets you open ./refinement_batch directly in the GUI (or via Pose Estimation Workbench → 3. Active Learning Outliers), drag only the mispredicted points, and merge the corrected frames back into your training set.

docs.title: Offline Pose Filtering & Bounded Gap Interpolation
docs.text:
Clean noisy predictions using p-cutoff masking, velocity-jump and anatomical bone-length outlier rejection, bounded linear/cubic/nearest gap interpolation, and zero-phase savgol, median, one_euro, or moving_average smoothing. When filtering a LabelMe directory, all non-point shapes (animal polygons, masks, and zones) are preserved intact.

annolid-run filter-pose ./pred_labelme \
  --pose-schema ./pose_schema.json \
  --min-confidence 0.5 \
  --max-jump-px 45 \
  --enforce-bone-bounds \
  --interpolate linear --max-gap 5 \
  --method savgol --window 5 \
  -o ./pred_filtered

docs.title: Multi-Animal Pose Identity Swap Repair
docs.text:
Swap two animals (updating both pose keypoints and parent polygons/bboxes consistently) from frame t forward — via Pose Estimation Workbench → 5. Labeled Video & Swap IDs, the canvas right-click menu (Swap Pose Instances Forward…), or CLI:

# Dry-run preview first
annolid-run swap-pose ./pred_labelme \
  --start-frame 420 --instance-a mouse_1 --instance-b mouse_2 --dry-run

# Apply swap from frame 420 to end of video
annolid-run swap-pose ./pred_labelme \
  --start-frame 420 --instance-a mouse_1 --instance-b mouse_2

Automatic repair via annolid-run repair-tracks (temporal continuity or Identity Governor) also keeps child pose keypoints synchronized when parent animal identities are corrected, and annolid-run track-qc (and Analysis & Reporting Studio → Track QC & Gaps) checks stretched bones, collapsed bones, and per-keypoint velocity spikes.

docs.title: 7. Calibrated Pose Kinematics (pose-kinematics)
docs.text:
Compute skeleton-level kinematics with optional orthographic (--px-per-cm) or planar homography (--calibration) calibration:

  • Per-keypoint speed, acceleration, distance, and coverage (keypoint_kinematics.csv)
  • Per-bone length distributions (bone_lengths.csv)
  • Auto-derived 3-point joint angles and angular velocities (joint_angles.csv, joint_angles_timeseries.csv)
  • Body heading and egocentric body-aligned coordinates (egocentric_pose.csv)
  • Inter-animal keypoint-pair distances, close contact, and directed bearings (dyadic_keypoints.csv)
annolid-run pose-kinematics ./pred_filtered \
  --pose-schema ./pose_schema.json \
  --fps 30 --px-per-cm 12.5 \
  --output-dir ./pose_kinematics_out

docs.title: 8. Render Labeled Skeleton Videos (render-pose-video)
docs.text:
Render deterministic, full-resolution skeleton overlay videos from any LabelMe, AnnotationStore, SLEAP, DeepLabCut, or Tracking CSV source (with optional raw-vs-filtered comparison markers):

annolid-run render-pose-video trial.mp4 ./pred_filtered \
  -o ./trial_labeled_pose.mp4 \
  --pose-schema ./pose_schema.json \
  --comparison ./pred_labelme \
  --color-mode instance \
  --min-confidence 0.5 \
  --trail-length 15 \
  --draw-labels

Supported --color-mode options: instance (per-animal high-contrast palette), bodypart (DLC-style per-keypoint palette), and confidence (red → amber → green score heatmap).

docs.title: DeepLabCut, SLEAP & External Pose Interoperability
docs.text:
Annolid provides bidirectional import and export for pose and keypoint tracking ecosystems used in behavioral neuroscience. For the complete end-to-end pose estimation workflow (k-means frame sampling, evaluation metrics, active-learning outliers, filtering/interpolation, pose kinematics, and labeled skeleton video export), see Pose Estimation Workflow.

Ecosystem / Format Import to Annolid Export from Annolid Notes DeepLabCut analysis (.csv, .h5) Single- & multi-animal (3- and 4-row headers), likelihood filtering, config.yaml skeleton 3-row (single-animal) & 4-row (multi-animal) CSV (--format deeplabcut-csv) & HDF5 (--format deeplabcut-h5) Auto-discovers *DLC_*.csv / *DLC_*.h5; reads and writes fixed-format .h5 via h5py (no PyTables required). DeepLabCut training (labeled-data/CollectedData_*.{csv,h5}) Single- & multi-animal CSV/H5, cross-platform paths, config.yaml edges, LabelMe-safe flags Full project (labeled-data/<video>/CollectedData_<scorer>.{csv,h5}, images, config.yaml) Round-trips cleanly with pose_schema.json and read_pose_dataset(). Lightning Pose (.csv, training projects) Uses DLC 3- and 4-row CSV format Same as DeepLabCut CSV / training project Use --format lightning-pose or --format auto. SLEAP projects (.slp, .pkg.slp) Multi-video, /tracks_json track names, point/instance scores, skeleton edges & symmetry, occluded keypoints .slp or self-contained .pkg.slp (--embed-images) Prefers user labels over overlapping predictions on the same frame by default. SLEAP Analysis HDF5 (.analysis.h5) /tracks, /node_names, /track_names, /edge_names, /point_scores, /instance_scores Standard SLEAP analysis HDF5 (tracks, point_scores, instance_scores, track_occupancy, edge_names, edge_inds) Requires h5py (pip install 'annolid[sleap]'). SimBA / B-SOiD / VAME / Keypoint-MoSeq / movement Standard DLC CSV or SLEAP .analysis.h5 --format deeplabcut-csv, --format simba, or --format sleap-h5 Directly readable from Annolid LabelMe folders, AnnotationStore NDJSON, or *_tracking.csv. COCO Keypoints (.json) Keypoints + skeleton edges (with bbox-center fallback) and optional pose_schema.json export COCO keypoints export with canonical PoseSchema order, 1-indexed skeleton edges, and coco2deeplabcut real DLC CSV export Preserves visibility (1=occluded, 2=visible) in both directions.

docs.title: DeepLabCut / Lightning Pose / SimBA
docs.text:
Open Tools → DeepLabCut / Lightning Pose Import & Export…:

  1. Import DLC / Lightning Pose analysis (CSV / H5 → LabelMe):
  2. Pick a .csv or .h5 file directly, or pick a video to auto-discover matching *DLC_*.csv / *DLC_*.h5.
  3. Single-animal (3 header rows) and multi-animal (4 header rows: scorer, individuals, bodyparts, coords) layouts are auto-detected.
  4. Optionally filter low-confidence predictions via Min likelihood and extract matching PNG frames.
  5. Import DLC / Lightning Pose training data:
  6. Select a labeled-data folder containing CollectedData_*.csv or CollectedData_*.h5.
  7. If a sibling config.yaml exists, Annolid reads its skeleton edges and body-part ordering into pose_schema.json.
  8. Export Annolid LabelMe / Tracking → DeepLabCut / Lightning Pose / SimBA:
  9. Select a LabelMe annotation directory (including *_annotations.ndjson AnnotationStore files) or an Annolid *_tracking.csv.
  10. Choose Analysis CSV (for DeepLabCut, Lightning Pose, SimBA, B-SOiD, VAME, or movement) or Training Project (labeled-data/ + config.yaml).

docs.title: SLEAP (.slp, .pkg.slp, .analysis.h5)
docs.text:
Open Tools → SLEAP (.slp / .h5) Import & Export…:

  1. Import SLEAP → LabelMe:
  2. Select a .slp, .pkg.slp, or .analysis.h5 file.
  3. Optionally supply an external video (for non-packaged .slp or .analysis.h5) or an existing pose_schema.json for keypoint name mapping.
  4. Choose whether to prefer user-labeled instances over overlapping predictions and whether to preserve occluded keypoints (visible=False with finite coordinates → COCO/Annolid kp_visibility=1).
  5. Export Annolid → SLEAP:
  6. Select a LabelMe folder or *_tracking.csv.
  7. Export to SLEAP Analysis HDF5 (.analysis.h5), SLEAP Project (.slp), or Self-Contained Package (.pkg.slp) with embedded frames.

docs.title: Direct Overlay Playback & Skeleton Visualization in the GUI
docs.text:
• Auto-discovery: Opening a video, an annotation directory, a labeled image, or a DeepLabCut/Lightning Pose overlay automatically loads a sibling pose_schema.json / .yaml / .yml (or project.annolid.json pose_schema_path, or a sibling DLC config.yaml skeleton) onto the canvas and Keypoint Sequencer.
  • Skeleton editing & presets: Both the Keypoint Sequencer dock and the New Project Wizard provide built-in species presets (Mouse 5/9/11 keypoints, Fly, Fish, Human COCO 17), anatomical edge auto-inference, combo-based and click-to-toggle skeleton edge editing, and an anatomical left/right-aligned skeleton preview.
  • Canvas rendering: When Show pose skeleton (edges) is enabled, bones are rendered with per-instance high-contrast colors in multi-animal scenes, dashed lines for occluded (kp_visibility=1) keypoints, skipped bones for missing (kp_visibility=0) keypoints, and emphasized strokes for selected or hovered keypoints.
  • DeepLabCut / Lightning Pose playback: When opening a video alongside a DeepLabCut or Lightning Pose analysis .csv or .h5 (single- or multi-animal), Annolid parses 3- and 4-level headers automatically and overlays labeled points and skeleton bones with multi-animal group_id, instance_label, and score metadata.
  • COCO Keypoints round-trip: Export LabelMe → COCO in keypoints mode accepts (or auto-discovers) a pose_schema.json to emit canonical keypoint ordering, 1-indexed COCO skeleton pairs, and kp_visibility; Convert COCO → LabelMe can write pose_schema.json alongside converted images so skeletons render immediately on open.

docs.title: Import External Pose Data (import-pose)
docs.text:
# Auto-detect DeepLabCut / Lightning Pose CSV or H5 (single- or multi-animal)
annolid-run import-pose trialDLC_dlcrnet_filtered.csv \
  --video trial.mp4 \
  --min-likelihood 0.5 \
  -o ./trial_labelme

# Import a SLEAP project (.slp / .pkg.slp) or SLEAP Analysis HDF5 (.analysis.h5)
annolid-run import-pose predictions.analysis.h5 \
  --video trial.mp4 \
  -o ./sleap_labelme

# Import a SLEAP .pkg.slp and generate an Annolid dataset index JSONL
annolid-run import-pose labels.pkg.slp \
  -o ./sleap_labelme \
  --write-index

# Import a DeepLabCut / Lightning Pose training project (legacy command also supported)
annolid-run import-deeplabcut-training-data \
  --source-dir /path/to/dlc_project \
  --labeled-data labeled-data \
  --write-pose-schema \
  --pose-schema-preset auto

docs.title: Export Annolid Annotations or Tracking (export-pose)
docs.text:
# Export LabelMe folder (or AnnotationStore) to DeepLabCut / Lightning Pose / SimBA CSV
annolid-run export-pose ./trial_labelme \
  --format deeplabcut-csv \
  --scorer my_lab \
  -o ./trial_dlc.csv

# Export LabelMe folder to a complete DeepLabCut / Lightning Pose training project
annolid-run export-pose ./trial_labelme \
  --format deeplabcut-project \
  --scorer my_lab \
  --video-name trial \
  -o ./dlc_project

# Export Annolid tracking CSV or LabelMe folder to SLEAP Analysis HDF5
annolid-run export-pose ./trial_tracking.csv \
  --format sleap-h5 \
  --video ./trial.mp4 \
  -o ./trial.analysis.h5

# Export LabelMe folder to a self-contained SLEAP .pkg.slp
annolid-run export-pose ./trial_labelme \
  --format sleap-slp \
  --embed-images \
  -o ./trial.pkg.slp

docs.title: COCO Keypoints to DeepLabCut CSV
docs.text: python -m annolid.annotation.coco2deeplabcut annotations.json output_dlc.csv --scorer my_lab

docs.title: Dependencies & Format Notes
docs.text:
• CSV formats (DeepLabCut / Lightning Pose / SimBA / Annolid tracking CSV) work with Annolid's core dependencies (pandas, PyYAML, Pillow).
  • HDF5 & ZIP formats (SLEAP HDF5 .slp / .pkg.slp / .analysis.h5, ZIP-based .slp archives, and DeepLabCut fixed & table format .h5) require h5py for HDF5 containers: 
    pip install "annolid[sleap]"
  • External HDF5 compression filters: Standard uncompressed, gzip, and lzf DeepLabCut .h5 files (both fixed and PyTables table formats) are read directly via h5py without requiring tables; files compressed with optional third-party filters such as blosc require hdf5plugin or tables (or use the sibling .csv).
  • LabelMe flag safety: Imported point shapes store boolean-only values in shape["flags"] (kp_visible, predicted) and keep string/numeric metadata (instance_label, display_label, kp_visibility, score) as top-level shape fields so LabelMe and Annolid GUI flag widgets never fail.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text: This page collects the current operational reference points for Annolid.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Primary entry points:

  • annolid: launch the GUI
  • annolid-run: run plugin-based training and inference workflows

Common CLI discovery commands:

annolid --help
annolid-run --help
annolid-run list-models
annolid-run help train
annolid-run help predict
annolid-run help train <model>
annolid-run help predict <model>

Model help details:

  • Built-in model plugins now show curated quick-reference groups before the full flag list.
  • Older forms such as annolid-run train <model> --help-model remain supported.
  • Plugin-author contract and examples: Model Plugin Help

Agent-side CLI execution:

  • Annolid Agent and annolid-run

Multi-animal track quality control, active-learning review queue, and headless track repair commands:

annolid-run track-qc ./session_frames/ --expected-instances 2 --pose-schema pose_schema.json --review-csv review_queue.csv --out track_qc.json
annolid-run repair-tracks ./session_frames/ --expected-instances 2
annolid-run repair-tracks ./session_frames/ --expected-instances 2 --apply
annolid-run repair-tracks ./session_frames/ --mode governor --policy policy.json --zones zones.json --apply

Behavior analytics, quality control, inter-rater reliability, and cohort aggregation commands:

annolid-run time-budget exported_events.csv --schema project.annolid.json -o time_budget.csv
annolid-run behavior-qc exported_events.csv --schema project.annolid.json --strict --out qc_report.json
annolid-run behavior-irr rater_1.csv rater_2.csv --schema project.annolid.json --bin-seconds 0.1 --csv-out irr_summary.csv
annolid-run behavior-cohort ./scored_csvs/ --metadata-csv unblind_key.csv --summary-csv cohort_summary.csv --transitions-csv cohort_transitions.csv

Security-focused agent commands:

annolid-run agent-security-check
annolid-run agent-security-audit
annolid-run agent-security-audit --fix
annolid-run agent-secrets-audit
annolid-run agent-box-auth-url --redirect-uri https://your-app.example.com/oauth/callback
annolid-run agent-box-auth-url --authorize-base-url https://my_org_xxx.account.box.com --redirect-uri https://your-app.example.com/oauth/callback
annolid-run agent-box-auth-url --open-browser --redirect-uri https://your-app.example.com/oauth/callback
annolid-run agent-box-auth-exchange --redirect-uri https://your-app.example.com/oauth/callback --code <auth_code>
annolid-run agent-box-auth-exchange --authorize-base-url https://my_org_xxx.account.box.com --redirect-uri https://your-app.example.com/oauth/callback --code <auth_code>
annolid-run agent-box-token-refresh

The Agent Runtime settings dialog includes Box auth host, client ID, client secret, and redirect URI fields so the GUI auth button can reuse the same values after Annolid restarts. The redirect URI defaults to http://localhost:8765/oauth/callback and includes a copy button for pasting into the Box app registration page. When that redirect points to localhost, Annolid starts a temporary local callback listener so Box can complete the OAuth round trip instead of showing a connection error page. Use http:// for localhost callbacks; https://localhost/... is not supported by the local listener.

ACP bridge command:

annolid-run agent acp bridge --workspace /path/to/repo

docs.title: Reporting, Statistics & Analysis Studio
docs.text: Annolid provides a unified stack for multi-animal track quality control, calibrated kinematics, freezing detection, spatial zone analysis, inter-rater reliability (IRR), inferential cohort statistics, and self-contained HTML5/SVG scientific reporting across the GUI, annolid-run CLI, and Annolid Bot tools.

docs.title: 1. GUI Workbench: Analysis & Reporting Studio
docs.text:
Open Analysis -> Analysis & Reporting Studio… (Ctrl+Shift+R) in the main Annolid window (or click Studio… from the Behavior Log dock).

The non-modal studio runs computations on background worker threads so the main video canvas stays responsive, and provides six integrated tabs:

  1. Unified Report: Generates analysis_report.html (with deterministic inline SVG arena trajectories, freezing/active budgets, zone occupancy bars, and BORIS-style ethogram rasters), analysis_report.md, and analysis_report.json (unified_analysis_report/v1).
  2. Track QC & Gaps: Audits tracking CSVs or frame JSON folders for velocity spikes, identity swaps, area jumps, pose bone stretch, and missing-frame gaps.
  3. Kinematics & Freezing: Computes physical (cm, cm/s via px_per_cm) and pixel kinematics, straightness/tortuosity, freezing & high-activity bouts, and pairwise inter-animal proximity.
  4. Behavior & Ethogram QC: Summarizes interval-union time budgets, binned trajectories, and unpaired/exclusive ethogram alerts.
  5. Inter-Rater Reliability (IRR): Evaluates 2+ rater event CSVs with Cohen's $\kappa$ (plus bootstrap 95% CI), Fleiss' $\kappa$, Krippendorff's $\alpha$, PABAK, bout onset/offset F1, and contiguous disagreement bouts.
  6. Cohort & Transitions: Computes between-group hypothesis tests, standardized effect sizes, Kaplan-Meier censored latency survival, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR $q$-values, and first-order Markov transition matrices.

Interactive Frame Navigation: Double-clicking any row in the Track QC review queue, Tracking Gaps, Kinematics Bouts, Behavior QC Alerts, or IRR Disagreements tables jumps the main Annolid canvas directly to that frame.

docs.title: Live Worked Example (mouse083_task1_annotator1)
docs.text:
Inspect an actual unified HTML5 + inline SVG report generated by annolid-run report on the 4,881-frame mouse083_task1_annotator1 resident-intruder assay:

  • Open live interactive HTML5/SVG report
  • Read the full mouse083 end-to-end walkthrough

docs.title: 2. annolid-run CLI Reference
docs.text:
# 1. Unified HTML5 + inline SVG + Markdown + JSON report
annolid-run report session.mp4 \
    --events-csv session_events.csv \
    --zone-file session_zones.json \
    --fps 30 \
    --px-per-cm 12.5 \
    --output-dir ./session_report

# 2. Calibrated trajectory kinematics, freezing bouts, and pairwise social distance
#    Supports scalar --px-per-cm OR planar perspective homography (--calibration)
annolid-run kinematics session_tracking.csv \
    --fps 30 \
    --calibration arena_calibration.json \
    --output-dir ./kinematics_out \
    --events-csv kinematics_bouts.csv

# 3. Spatial zone / place-preference / social summary (polygons, rectangles, and 2-point circles)
annolid-run zone-analysis session.mp4 \
    --zone-file session_zones.json \
    --profile open_field \
    --mode assay_summary \
    --events-csv zone_visits.csv

# 4. Standalone anatomical body-part posture & directed contact ethogram
annolid-run body-part-ethogram ./session/ \
    --fps 30 \
    --output-prefix ./ethogram/session \
    --events-csv body_part_events.csv

# 5. Per-instance tracking gap report (works on videos, tracking CSVs, or JSON folders)
annolid-run gap-report session_tracking.csv --fps 30 --out-json gaps.json

# 6. Multi-video *_tracking_stats.json telemetry dashboard
annolid-run tracking-stats ./project_videos/ --output-dir ./stats_dashboard

# 7. Behavior time budget with BORIS Out-of-Sight subtraction, external photometry/sensor alignment, & SVG/DOT
annolid-run time-budget session_events.csv \
    --schema project.annolid.json \
    --session-duration 600 \
    --exclude-behaviors out_of_sight,occluded \
    --bin-size 60 \
    --external-data photometry_dff.csv \
    --external-offset 0.25 \
    --external-data-svg photometry_aligned.svg \
    --cooccurrence-csv cooccurrence.csv \
    --ethogram-svg ethogram.svg \
    --transitions-dot transitions.dot \
    --transitions-svg transitions.svg \
    -o time_budget.csv

# 8. Bidirectional BORIS (.boris / Tabular CSV / Aggregated CSV) import & export
annolid-run boris-import study.boris \
    --output-dir ./annolid_from_boris \
    --group-variable Treatment

annolid-run boris-export session_events.csv \
    --schema project.annolid.json \
    --format boris \
    --output session.boris

# 9. Inter-Rater Reliability with bootstrap 95% CIs, Krippendorff's alpha, and disagreement CSV
annolid-run behavior-irr rater1.csv rater2.csv \
    --bin-seconds 0.1 \
    --disagreements-csv disagreements.csv \
    --out irr_report.json

# 10. Multi-recording cohort inferential comparisons & transition diagrams
annolid-run behavior-cohort ./annolid_from_boris/cohort_manifest.json \
    --unit recording \
    --session-duration 600 \
    --summary-csv cohort_summary.csv \
    --comparisons-csv cohort_comparisons.csv \
    --transitions-csv cohort_transitions.csv \
    --transitions-dot cohort_transitions.dot \
    --transitions-svg cohort_transitions.svg \
    --out cohort_report.json

docs.title: 3. Inferential Cohort & IRR Methods
docs.text:
• Experimental Unit (--unit recording vs --unit subject): In dyadic or group-housed recordings (resident + intruder), co-housed animals share variance. Setting --unit recording aggregates within-recording totals/rates first so recordings act as the independent experimental unit.
  • Hypothesis Tests & Effect Sizes (CohortComparisonRow):
  • 2 groups: Welch's unequal-variance $t$-test, Mann-Whitney $U$, Hedges' $g$, Cliff's $\delta$, bootstrap 95% CI on mean difference, Fisher exact / $\chi^2$ responder incidence test, and Mantel-Cox log-rank test on right-censored first-bout latencies.
  • 3+ groups: One-way ANOVA $F$-test, Kruskal-Wallis $H$-test, Pearson $\chi^2$ responder contingency test, and $k$-sample Mantel-Cox log-rank test. All parametric, nonparametric, contingency, and survival tail probabilities include exact pure-Python/NumPy incomplete-beta and incomplete-gamma engines (_betainc_reg, _gammaincc_reg) so 2-group and $\ge 3$-group p-values remain exact even when scipy is not installed.
  • Multiple Comparisons: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR-adjusted $q$-values (q_parametric_bh, q_nonparametric_bh) across all behavior endpoints.
  • Spatial Calibration (px_per_cm & Planar Perspective Homography):
  • Uniform orthographic scale via --px-per-cm <float>, or full $3 \times 3$ planar perspective homography via --calibration <file.json> (PlanarCalibration in annolid.postprocessing.spatial_calibration).
  • Calibration JSON files may specify {"src_points_px": [[x1,y1], ...], "width_cm": 50.0, "height_cm": 50.0}, arbitrary $\ge 4$-point correspondences {"src_points_px": [...], "dst_points_cm": [...]}, an explicit $3 \times 3$ "homography" matrix, or a LabelMe/Annolid _zones.json shape with flags: {"width_cm": 50.0, "height_cm": 50.0}. Areas in cm^2 are scaled by the exact local projective Jacobian determinant $|\det J_H(x, y)|$.
  • Inter-Rater Reliability (IRRReport):
  • Pairwise Cohen's $\kappa$ with block-bootstrap 95% confidence intervals, multi-rater Fleiss' $\kappa$, prevalence-adjusted PABAK, binary Krippendorff's $\alpha$, onset/offset matching F1, and exported IRRDisagreementBout windows for targeted adjudication.
